542649|2026-06.headline: RVNL Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA nearly doubled to INR 171 crore (margin 3.99% vs 2.08%) on turnover up 9.62% to INR 4,300 crore.
542649|2026-06.overview: Standalone turnover rose 9.62% YoY to INR 4,300 crore and consolidated turnover rose 10.55% to INR 4,321 crore. Standalone EBITDA more than doubled to INR 171 crore, with PAT up 21.72% to INR 155 crore. Order inflow in the quarter was INR 5,417 crore, taking the total order book to INR 93,492 crore as on 30 June 2026. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% top-line growth and 15-20% bottom-line growth, and flagged labour shortages, client payment delays and geopolitics as challenges.

542650|2026-03.headline: Metropolis Q4 FY26 organic revenue grew 14.7% to INR 392 crores, with organic EBITDA margin at 27.2%, up from 18.5%.
542650|2026-03.overview: Organic revenue grew 14.7% YoY in Q4 FY26 to INR 392 crores, driven by 9.3% patient volume growth and about 5% realisation improvement, with no price increase taken in the quarter due to GST reasons. Organic EBITDA margin rose to 27.2% (from 18.5%) and full-year organic margin reached 25.9%, up about 140 bps after adjusting for prior-year acquisition costs. Management said the heavy lab and centre build-out is largely done, so the focus shifts to throughput-led productivity, and it guided to 14% to 15% revenue CAGR and a 27% to 28% group EBITDA margin over three years. Core Diagnostics reached a high-single-digit margin in Q4, meeting the 4-quarter turnaround commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Will you take a price hike this fiscal, and what margin improvement is achievable next year?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 14% to 15% growth comes from volume versus realisation?

542650|2026-06.headline: Metropolis Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR 450 crore with EBITDA margin up 210 bps to 25.2%, driven mostly by volume.
542650|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 17% YoY to INR 450 crore, ahead of guidance, with 10% patient volume and 11% test volume growth and no price increase in 18 months. EBITDA rose 27% YoY to INR 113 crore (25.2% margin, +210 bps) and PAT rose 26% to INR 57 crore (12.6% margin, +90 bps). Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 14-15% and a 100-150 bps EBITDA margin improvement, with a 27-28% margin target over the next two years. Network expansion continued (300 centers added in Q1, 500+ planned), while the company pruned about 300 low-productivity centers.

segments.name: Specialty Diagnostics
segments.commentary: 40% of Q1 revenue, +17% YoY; target to lift share to 45% from 40%. Genomics portfolio doubled over the past year.

segments.name: Core Diagnostics
segments.commentary: Margin in high single digits (~8% at Q4 FY26 end); target ~25% EBITDA margin within 3-4 years of acquisition. Effective acquisition multiple ~10x FY27 EBITDA per management.

qa_highlights.question: Split of patient volume growth between B2B and B2C, and colour on strong Q1 volume despite seasonally weak quarter and delayed monsoon.
qa_highlights.answer: B2C patient volume grew about 13.5% and B2B about 6%. Management attributed Q1 strength to market-access execution and seasonal momentum, but could not fully dissect it; possible overflow from Q4 was one theory.

qa_highlights.question: Does Metropolis run O&M or regional lab management with standalone labs, with profit-share arrangements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it already runs a lab-on-lease model for about 10 years, taking over pathologist-run labs fully. Number of such labs was not given; to be followed up.

qa_highlights.question: Is the TruHealth Mind and Body initiative a blend of genomics and advanced radiology, and what growth is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: TruHealth combines blood tests with vitals, basic radiology (X-ray, ECG, sonography) and cognitive/mental health checks. Genomics is not part of it yet. No package-level targets were set.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the business is CGHS and did it benefit Metropolis from the CGHS price revision?
qa_highlights.answer: CGHS is about 1% of revenue, so the one-time price revision benefit is small. Management expects CGHS empanelment to keep growing, though the one-time benefit will not recur next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance of 14-15% growth conservative, and is Q1 a one-off versus the base-rate growth of peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 14-15% for the year, citing a track record of delivering that range over the last two quarters. It declined to focus on quarter-by-quarter seasonality, noting weather-driven unpredictability.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 group capex was INR 65 crore and FY27 is expected to be in a similar range, including acquired entities.

qa_highlights.question: How will the 27-28% margin target be split between cost pressures and productivity gains, given Tier-2/3 expansion and raw-material pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not expand beyond 750 towns and has halted lab expansion for about five quarters, so new towns and labs should not add margin stress. It relies on operating leverage and productivity gains. Tier-2/3 economics were said to be no worse than metros.

542651|2026-03.headline: KPIT Q4 FY26 revenue grew 1.8% in constant currency and 12% YoY in rupees; management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of 20.5-21.2% as two large SDV programs ramp down.

542652|2026-03.overview: Management reported record annual and quarterly revenue, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 27% YoY and PAT of INR 7.9 bn (up 7%, 8.9% margin). Growth was price-led: cumulative price hikes of 18-19% were taken from January to March, while Cable & Wire volumes grew low single digits in the quarter. Middle East escalation, PVC price spikes and pollution-related construction halts hit March, which is the key month of Q4. FY26 was a record year: revenue above INR 285 bn (+29%), EBITDA margin 13.9%, PAT above INR 27 bn (+32%), and FY26 volume growth of 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Cable & Wire volume growth and price hikes taken from January?

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the Middle East disruption in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary sales were hit as distributors lifted less, since secondary sales did not move at the expected pace. Private sector demand was hit by gas rationing, and PVC prices rose 60-80% in early March. The impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Institutional mix and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutional sales were about 2-3 points higher than channel in Q4 (about 13-14% of the Cable & Wire top line in Q4 per management's arithmetic). Channel margins are 3-4% higher.

qa_highlights.question: Peak utilisation and capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-76%. Management says early 90s has been reached at times, but 80-85% is the sustainable level, and there is room for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Use of surplus cash and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains on capex funded from internal accruals and on the dividend payout. M&A is being evaluated in India and abroad, but nothing is in view for the near to mid term.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a firm number, but expects exports to exceed the current 5.4% share. US distribution was re-established and North America was about 40% of FY26 exports. Middle East was about 15-16% of FY26 exports and is not expected to contribute meaningfully in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory gains and raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there are no inventory gains or losses because raw materials are hedged for copper and aluminium, and copper is largely imported. XLPE and compound availability is comfortable for about one quarter, with a diversified vendor base.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable & Wire Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+, and above the 13.9% company level for FY26. FMEG was mid-single digit for both Q4 and FY26.

542652|2026-06.headline: Polycab Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 39% YoY, record PAT of INR 7,967 million (+33% YoY), EBITDA margin 13.8%.
542652|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 39% YoY with EBITDA up 32% and margin at 13.8%, about 70 bps sequentially higher. Record quarterly PAT of INR 7,967 million at a 9.7% margin. Wires & Cables grew 39% and FMEG grew 71%, while EPC revenue fell 11%. Volume growth in domestic cables and wires was low to mid-single digit against a high base of about 26% last year, and exports declined on the Middle East disruption. Management cut prices by 3-4% in early July and said channel destocking followed the sharp fall in copper and aluminium prices in June.

qa_highlights.answer: Domestic cable and wire volume grew low to mid-single digit on a high base; no Q2 copper guidance given, as pricing is cost-plus. A 3-4% price revision was taken in early July.

qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about 100-110 days, LC-based payables about 80-90 days, and receivables 20-30 days, producing a 15-day cycle this quarter. The accounting treatment was deferred to an offline discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre and optical fibre opportunity, and export trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres could add about INR 3.5 crores of cable per MW, an INR 20,000-25,000 crore market over 6-8 years, and Polycab already supplies conventional cables to some existing sites. Exports are recovering with a healthy order book; Middle East was 20-24% of Q1 exports.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Net fibre price risk and why EPC revenue fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre for the execution period is already secured, so Bharat Net is not exposed to higher fibre prices. EPC revenue timing is milestone-linked and may shift between quarters, with no material full-year dip expected.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume growth outlook and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 10-12 month trends rather than quarters; FY26 volume growth was 18% and 1.5x market growth is reiterated. Share gains of 3-4% were reported in the last update, with the next analysis expected after peers report.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of channel stocking benefiting Q1, and is the margin improvement limited?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking was below expectation as raw-material prices fell in June. Margins were supported by wires mix and channel mix, offset by weaker exports and operating leverage; the company targets the 11-13% range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG margin trajectory, and is 8% EBIT sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were operating leverage on a low base, a premium mix of about 25% overall, and regional product strategies. Management expects seasonality and targets 8-10% EBITDA margin for FMEG for full year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the data-centre and T&D demand strong enough to move industry growth, given the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that 1 GW of data-centre additions alone would be limited, but said T&D demand is accelerating, with about 15% cable content in T&D spend and transformer makers' order books at about 2.5x revenue.

542652|2026-09.headline: Polycab Q2 FY27 revenue rose 53% YoY with PAT of INR 9,900 million (+43%) and EBITDA margin of 14.4%, all record highs.

EBITDA rose 39% YoY to a 14.4% margin, up more than 50 bps QoQ, helped by mix, operating leverage and copper price pass-through. Wires and Cables grew 47% and FMEG grew 124%, with FMEG crossing a 10% EBIT margin for the first time. Management said the Asier Metals IBC matter is under NCLAT review, with order reserved and no material impact expected.

542665|2026-03.headline: Neogen Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 247 crore with 17.8% EBITDA margin; FY27 standalone guidance INR 875-950 crore.
542665|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 247 crore, almost entirely volume-driven, with EBITDA up 21% to INR 44 crore and margin at 17.8% despite Dahej replacement and toll manufacturing costs. PAT was INR 11 crore for the quarter and INR 29 crore for FY26 on revenue of INR 862 crore. Battery materials (Neogen Ionics) remain the core growth push: Dahej Phase 1 is budgeted at INR 428 crore and Pakhajan Phase 2 revised to INR 1,367 crore, with commissioning now guided within FY27. 542665|2026-06.headline: Neogen Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR 250 crore, EBITDA up 53% to INR 48 crore, with margin at 19.3%.
542665|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR 250 crore grew 34% YoY, led by organo-lithium, inorganic chemicals and battery chemicals, with record quarterly revenue in organo-lithium and battery chemicals. EBITDA rose 53% to INR 48.2 crore and margin expanded 260 bps to 19.3% despite Dahej rebuild, toll manufacturing and Neogen Ionics start-up costs. PAT rose 67% to INR 17.1 crore. Management raised standalone FY27 revenue guidance to INR 950-1,050 crore from INR 875-950 crore and approved a INR 600 crore QIP mainly for debt reduction.

542726|2026-09.headline: IndiaMART Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 429 crore, with EBITDA margin of 37% and paying suppliers down 615 QoQ to 2,17,000.
542726|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to Rs 429 crore and consolidated collections grew 9% to Rs 443 crore, while deferred revenue rose 16% to Rs 2,029 crore. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 159 crore (37% margin) and net profit was Rs 91 crore, with other income negative at Rs 8 crore due to bond-yield MTM losses. Paying suppliers fell by 615 QoQ to 2,17,000, attributed mainly to elevated Silver subscription churn. Management said unique business enquiries and active buyers have declined for about two quarters, which it linked to AI-driven search changes and its own decision to restrict data access, with a 10-15% loss from peak levels.

financial_highlights.change: Due to MTM losses from bond yield increase; management calls it notional

segments.name: IndiaMART marketplace
segments.commentary: Collections Rs 394 crore (+8% YoY) standalone; 27 million unique business enquiries in Q2; paying suppliers 2,17,000 after net decline of 615 in the quarter. Gold and Platinum are about 50% of customers and about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: BUSY Infotech
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations Rs 37 crore (+27% YoY), billing Rs 46 crore (+20% YoY), deferred revenue about Rs 155 crore (+40% YoY), cash from operations about Rs 12 crore. About 11,000 new licences sold in Q2, taking the total to 4,66,000.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 33% reiterated; management called it conservative, and Q2 margin was 37% on a consolidated basis.

Management said margins are not comparable quarter to quarter because costs are upfront and revenue recognised over up to 18 months; it plans to invest more heavily in sales once Silver churn is better understood.
Management expects value and volume growth to be balanced over the next 2-3 years, versus historically about 10% value and 10% volume growth.
BUSY said comparable growth from Q3 onwards should be in line with the 20-30% overall growth rate it has been seeing.
No guidance on when Silver churn will improve; management has stopped giving that guidance.
capex_capacity: Management said 100% of expenses, including manpower and AI research, are expensed; no subsidiary capitalises manpower or software costs.
Advertising spend running at Rs 8-9 crore per quarter, nearing a Rs 10 crore per quarter budget, focused on the top quartile of categories.
Pilots underway for credit facilitation (IndiaMART Finance) and a paid verified business buyer programme; no significant capital committed yet.
Next ESOP pool decision to be taken by the board at financial year end; last pools were in 2018, 2022 and 2025.
demand_pricing: Unique business enquiries and active buyers have declined YoY for about two quarters; management attributes 10-15% loss from best-ever highs to Google AI Overviews and to restricting proprietary data behind logins.
Management said ARPU growth has historically run 5-10% and revenue growth is now 8-10%; growth has come mostly from value (ARPU and upsell) rather than volume over the last two to three years.
Silver 12-month retention is about 10% lower than four to five years ago, which management cites as the main gap to 10% volume and 10% value growth.
Around 10% of buyer traffic now comes through paid advertising, with 20-40% cannibalisation of organic traffic depending on the area.
Trust Assurance programme protects buyers up to Rs 5 lakh on purchases from verified bank accounts and TrustSEAL suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Why are active buyers and unique business enquiries declining, and is GenAI search a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: AI Overviews now cover 50% or more of searches, causing a 10-15% decline from peak. It has put more data behind logins and stopped showing some proprietary data to search engines and LLMs, and it accepts losing 10-20% of current enquiries to protect data.

qa_highlights.question: Is IndiaMART moving toward a transaction marketplace, as JustDial reportedly aspires to?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not going fully marketplace or away from listings, but wants to get closer to transactions, citing its earlier Tolexo and payment platform attempts and its current credit facilitation work.

qa_highlights.question: Where is AI showing up in the business, and is it monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 20+ AI use cases and voice AI serving 80,000-100,000 buyers daily, and said benefits are cost, intelligence and time. It said net benefit is volatile over 2-4 years and it does not expect AI to show up directly in enquiries yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ESOP cost fall, and what is the outlook for personnel cost leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Jitin Diwan said ESOP expense declines each year under the graded design, and the current level is the baseline until the next pool. Management said near-term AI experimentation adds cost and savings are reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the lending and credit facilitation business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to support marketplace transactions for high-value equipment, not to become a lender. Pilots are small and will be reported quarterly; no pre-approved credit lines yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for BUSY collection growth, which has appeared to decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Brijesh Agrawal said Q1 and Q2 FY27 growth was inflated by a higher base from a billing methodology change and customer win-back in the prior year; comparable growth should be 20-30% from Q3.

risks_watch: Paying supplier base declined by 615 QoQ; Silver churn has not yet improved and no timeline is given.
Unique enquiries and active buyers are down 10-15% from peak, with AI search and data restrictions cited as the drivers.
Other income is negative (Rs 8 crore) from bond MTM losses; management expects reversal over the next few quarters.
Credit facilitation and buyer monetisation programmes are at pilot stage with undefined capital and first-loss exposure.
Margin of 37% in Q2 reflects low sales investment; management plans to step up sales spend, which could compress margin.
542726|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on margins, the balance sheet and AI deployment, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Silver churn, buyer volume trends, timing of recovery and credit business economics, repeatedly saying outcomes are unknown and that it will report when results are material.
key_quotes: So yes, 10%, 15% decline on that is happening.
We are very certain, and we are not experimenting.
Nobody can predict next two, three quarters or next two, three years.
100% of our expense are expensed out, whether it is in the manpower, whether it is in the AI research or anywhere else.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Credit facilitation (IndiaMART Finance) and a paid verified business buyer programme are in pilot with no significant capital committed and no pre-approved credit lines yet.

rows.label: BUSY comparable growth of 20-30% from Q3

rows.label: Sales spend step-up after Silver churn is understood
rows.why: Advertising is Rs 8-9 crore per quarter, near the Rs 10 crore budget, and management plans heavier sales investment, so expenses rise against a 37% Q2 margin.

rows.label: Other income reversal from bond MTM losses
rows.why: Consolidated other income is negative Rs 8 crore from bond-yield MTM losses, which management calls notional and expects to reverse over the next few quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, the Rs 3,234 crore treasury and AI deployment, but cautious and evasive on Silver churn, buyer volume decline and credit business economics; analysts pressed on GenAI search cannibalisation and the marketplace/transaction strategy.

542752|2026-03.headline: Affle 3i Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20.3% y-o-y to INR 7.24 billion; FY26 revenue INR 27.1 billion (+19.5%) and EBITDA margin 22.5%.
542752|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 7.24 billion grew 20.3% y-o-y and 1% q-o-q, marking a 13th consecutive quarter of sequential growth despite geopolitical softness. EBITDA was INR 1.61 billion (22.3% margin, broadly flat y-o-y margin), and PAT was INR 1.20 billion (+16% y-o-y), held back by a low tax base in Q4 FY25. For FY26, revenue was INR 27.1 billion, EBITDA INR 6.10 billion (+26.3%) and PAT INR 4.55 billion (+19.1%). Management said inventory and data costs are rising as a deliberate investment in premium, verticalized inventory, and a roughly one-year investment phase is expected before margins improve. The board approved a preferential warrant issue to Affle Holdings (~INR 11 billion, 25% upfront) to fund acquisitions expected to be concluded within the calendar year.

+16.0% y-o-y, +0.2% q-o-q; subdued by low Q4 FY25 tax rate

segments.commentary: Contributed 71.6% of revenue and grew 21.2% y-o-y; on an adjusted basis India grew 19.5% and Emerging Markets 22.3% y-o-y.

segments.commentary: Contributed 28.4% of revenue, growing 18.0% y-o-y; management describes this region as under-calibrated and a focus for investment.

Combined entity (post-acquisition) targeted to average around 20% growth with EBITDA margin of about 23% to 25% over time.
Inventory and data costs expected to stay range-bound within the unit economic model; investment phase expected to last about one more year, after which margins should improve progressively.
Management says it will take an acquisition of a meaningful size within the calendar year 2026; may do more than one transaction through FY27.
Modelling 2% long-term average inflation in planning.
capex_capacity: Preferential issue: Affle Holdings to acquire ~7.4 million warrants at INR 1,487 each, totalling ~INR 11 billion, with 25% paid upfront, subject to shareholder approval.
Management says the company already holds substantial cash; the warrant route was chosen to show certainty of funds during deal negotiations.

Around 10 companies evaluated and about 4 shortlisted for deeper due diligence; target profile is a company with a direct advertiser base, sales team and existing integrations in developed markets (North America, Europe).
Past acquisitions (2020-2023) were loss-making or breakeven and have been converted to the CPCU model; management expects a 1-3 year conversion timeline for any new target.
Borrowings being repaid; cash balance accumulating per management.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 was affected by geopolitical softness in select markets and verticals; Jan-Mar is seasonally weaker with no festive quarter benefit.
Management says ~75% of revenue goes direct to advertisers; 25%+ comes through large ad agency group partners, with direct integration to the advertiser app still required.
Management argues the competitive edge is direct advertiser integration, verticalization and CPCU model; sees no significant change in competitor landscape.
CPCU pricing has risen over the last 10 years per management; premium, high lifetime value targeting (premium devices, CTV, premium placements) is the stated reason for higher inventory costs.
Management declined to share repeat-customer percentages or names; says engagement is cyclical, typically budget-to-budget.
Q4 inventory and data costs were 63.3% of revenue, up ~90 bps q-o-q; gross margin has declined over the last 7-8 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin declining for the last 7-8 quarters, and is it competition, mix or conscious investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a conscious investment in verticalization, premium inventory, CTV and first-party data integration, mainly in developed markets. Management expects roughly one year more of investment before benefits and a return toward better margin levels.

qa_highlights.question: Ticket size and asset focus for M&A (reference ~USD 200 million)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a size; deals range from small to larger. It said the company is ready to execute in the short term but will be patient on price and terms.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for an acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a meaningfully sized transaction is realistically possible within the calendar year, with no firm timeline until definitive agreements are near.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% organic growth too conservative given AI tailwinds, and how does 10x fit with inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20% organic is a calibrated plan, not base effect. Faster growth would bring lower-quality revenue; the company declines some orders it judges unprofitable. Management expects the combined entity to average around 20% growth with 23-25% EBITDA margins over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why a warrant route rather than QIP, and what is Affle Holdings' funding source?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash is already substantial and the warrants provide certainty of funds during negotiations. It said it is an Affle 3i matter and any Affle Holdings funding notification would be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses fell ~3% in FY26 and other income fell ~17%; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the other-expense decline mainly to lower business promotion spend, which is concentrated in Q1-Q3. Other income declined from treasury, with exchange gains and lower cash from debt repayment.

542752|2026-06.headline: Affle 3i Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20.4% y-o-y to INR 7.47 billion with EBITDA of INR 1.68 billion (22.4% margin), though management flagged RMG and FinTech headwinds.

EBITDA rose 20% y-o-y to INR 1.68 billion with margin at 22.4%, and PAT grew 21.7% y-o-y to INR 1.28 billion. Management said over 95% of revenue grew above 25% y-o-y after adjusting for regulatory and macro headwinds in RMG and some FinTech categories. Operating cash flow to PAT was weak in the quarter, which management attributed to timing of collections after a strong March 2026. The company reiterated a 10x growth plan with a larger acquisition targeted to close by early 2027.

542759|2026-03.headline: Spandana returned to profit in Q4 FY26 with PAT of INR5 crore, ending six loss-making quarters, as AUM grew 12% QoQ to INR4,420 crore.
542759|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 marked the first quarterly profit after six quarters, with PAT of INR5 crore versus a loss of INR95 crore in Q3 and PBT of INR8 crore versus a loss of INR125 crore. AUM rose 12% QoQ to INR4,420 crore, the first AUM increase after eight quarters, with disbursements up to about INR500 crore per month from INR400 crore in Q3. Opex fell to about INR161 crore from INR195 crore, and PPOP rose to INR39 crore from INR8 crore. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 3.8% (4.2% in Dec-25), NNPA at 0.73% and X-bucket collection efficiency at 99.7%. NIM contracted to 9.9% from 11.1% as borrowing costs stayed high.

segments.commentary: Disbursements averaged about INR500 crore per month in Q4 versus INR400 crore in Q3 and INR300 crore in Q2. About 80% of AUM is now under the new BRE and guardrails, with 99.7% X-bucket collection efficiency. 542760|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue hit a record INR7,548 crore (+20% YoY) and Q4 PAT a record INR142 crore, but FY26 net loss of INR296 crore after INR611 crore exceptional litigation charges.
542760|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 turnover of INR7,548 crore, up 20% YoY, and record quarterly PAT of INR142 crore in Q4 FY26. Q4 revenue fell both sequentially and YoY to INR1,946 crore because commodity volatility forced deferral of some supplies and execution plans. FY26 order inflow was over INR10,000 crore (EPC inflow up 43% YoY to INR10,062 crore), taking unexecuted order value (UOV) to a record INR11,813 crore. Management guided to about 15% revenue and order growth in FY27 and excluded any Reliance New Energy orders from that view.

segments.commentary: International revenue was INR1,444 crore in FY26 with UOV of about INR2,562 crore. Gross margin reached 13.2% in FY26 (vs 8% in FY25), helped by three projects commissioned under budgeted cost in Q4. Two South Africa projects were won for US$270 million.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Total O&M portfolio rose to 13.5 GW from 8.7 GW a year earlier. Management expects gross margin to stabilise around 20%; a roughly 900 MW O&M order from Serentica was won in Q4.

segments.commentary: FY26 included one pure BESS order of 790 MWh. About INR300 crore of current UOV is battery-related, and management expects about 20% of new orders to come from BESS, at 8-10% gross margin.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said deep engagement continues on technology and configuration and that traction should come in FY27, but gave no timing for the quarter, no order size and no margins. Reliance is excluded from the 15% growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 FY26 margin improvement a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Ajit Pratap Singh said three international projects near completion delivered savings over budgeted cost; this is not a recurring margin level, and the 8-10% EPC guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the exposure in the US litigation cases, and could the loss be larger than INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has about INR200 crore out of pocket, largely backed by a promoter indemnity. Management could not quantify additional litigation or penalty costs if cases are lost, saying the outcome is expected to take about 2 years, and the chance of losing is 'very remote'.

qa_highlights.question: How will the bank rating and credit lines affect the business?

542760|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR1,590 crores on slow international execution, while UOV hit a record INR13,000 crores and guidance was trimmed to 10-15% growth.
542760|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR1,590 crores, lower both sequentially and year-on-year, mainly from lower execution in the international EPC segment as four overseas projects neared completion. Gross margin was about 9.9% versus 10.5% in FY26, operational EBITDA was INR78 crores (4.9% margin), and reported EBITDA of INR96 crores included forex gains; PAT rose 36% YoY to INR53 crores on lower tax. Unexecuted order value (UOV) reached a record INR13,000 crores after a Egypt West Minya award (about USD560 million), and O&M portfolio grew to 18.3 GW. Management cut its FY27 top-line growth view to 10-15% (from about 15%), pushing the revenue ramp into H2 and expecting Q2 to be similarly slow.

542812|2026-09.headline: GFL Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 45% YoY to INR1,760 crores, with EBITDA up 32% to INR473 crores at a steady 27% margin.
542812|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR1,760 crores (+45% YoY, +11% QoQ) and EBITDA INR473 crores (+32% YoY, +11% QoQ), with PAT of INR240 crores (+42% YoY). Fluorochemicals revenue more than doubled YoY to INR607 crores, led by R-32 refrigerants, while fluoropolymers grew 22% YoY to INR931 crores. Battery materials (GFCL EV) remains pre-commercial, with LiPF6 ramping and LFP, electrolyte and anode timelines pushed out, and the INR6,000 crore battery capex plan is being funded partly by external equity still to be raised.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals (refrigerants)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR607 crores, +135% YoY, driven by R-32; management expects initial R-32 capacity to be fully utilised by end of Q3 FY27 and R-134A production to start by Q4 FY27. Refrigerant demand and pricing described as stable near term.

segments.name: Bulk chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR151 crores, -5% YoY and -8% QoQ, due to lower caustic soda prices and higher captive use of chloromethanes for R-32.

segments.name: Advanced battery materials (GFCL EV)
segments.commentary: Pre-commercial; LiPF6 supplied to 5 global electrolyte players with volume-linked, formula-priced contracts. Revenue from LFP, electrolyte and anode is pushed out; no revenue figure disclosed in the call.

LiPF6: expanded capacity expected to reach full utilisation by Q1 FY28; salt capacities near full utilisation by Q1/Q2 FY28.
Electrolyte: domestic demand expected to ramp from mid-CY27; revenue expected in H2 FY28; no new electrolyte capacity planned for about 6 months.
LFP: significant capacity to come online around Q3 FY28 or end FY28, with revenue impact at end FY28 or start FY29. Oman project put on hold and shifted to India.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the fluoropolymer 22% growth is volume versus price, and is 20% growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Malhotra said the 22% growth is volume-led and also reflects higher value from newly approved applications, and that growth momentum is expected to continue for a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: When will R-32 reach peak utilisation and when does R-134A start?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr Kapoor said initial R-32 capacity will be fully utilised by end of Q3 FY27 and R-134A production is on track for Q4 FY27; no utilisation percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR3,000+ crore FY27 capex be split and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-battery capex of INR800 crores is about halfway done, battery capex of INR2,100 crores is slipping about 1.5 quarters, and the total battery plan remains INR6,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is electrolyte and anode revenue timing later, and what is the sequence?

542830|2026-03.headline: IRCTC FY26 revenue from operations rose 11.55% to Rs 5,215 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 27.33% on exceptional items.
542830|2026-03.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue from operations (Rs 5,215 crore, up 11.55%), total revenue (Rs 5,475 crore, up 11.64%), PBT (Rs 1,875 crore, up 6.72%) and EBITDA (Rs 1,666 crore, up 7.48%). Q4 revenue from operations rose 15.05% YoY to Rs 1,460 crore, but Q4 profit fell to Rs 447 crore from Rs 472 crore, weighed by exceptional items (CSR, ECL provisioning) and a prior-year Rs 48 crore legacy income item not repeating. Management attributed the Q4 margin dip to exceptional items, saying margin would be about 30% excluding them. Catering and tourism grew fast while the internet ticketing segment grew slower. The call was led by the Director (Tourism and Marketing) because the Director (Finance) was unavailable.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 1,536 crore (+7.71%), profit +7.55%. Q4 revenue Rs 390 crore (+4.56%) with EBITDA margin 76%; Q4 EBIT margin 76% vs 85% due to CSR (additional Rs 17 crore), direct costs (~Rs 8 crore) and UPI share (~Rs 8 crore). Claims 89% share of reserved rail tickets.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 890 crore (+19.46%), profit +36.17%. Q4 revenue Rs 304 crore (+10.95%), EBITDA margin 16%; management said margin would be about 18% without CSR (Rs 1.5 crore) and lower margin on two Tejas Express trains.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 391 crore (+3.17%), profit +21.74%. Q4 revenue Rs 95 crore (+3.26%) with margin improvement attributed to favourable preform (PET) rates and material cost economies.

qa_highlights.question: What exceptional items hit Q4 and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Prior-year Rs 48 crore legacy income not repeated; CSR booked Rs 31 crore vs Rs 7 crore last year (incremental ~Rs 24 crore); ECL provision Rs 16 crore vs Rs 8 crore last year. Other expenses were about Rs 109 crore vs a typical Rs 40-50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did catering and internet ticketing EBIT margins fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited exceptional items: catering ECL Rs 16 crore (vs Rs 5 crore), CSR Rs 5 crore (vs Rs 1 crore), legacy item absent (Rs 33 crore last year), and about Rs 3 crore GST impact. For ticketing: CSR +Rs 17 crore, direct costs ~Rs 8 crore, UPI share ~Rs 8 crore. Analyst confirmed CSR and ECL sit in EBIT.

qa_highlights.question: Why was CSR booked in Q4 and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: CSR is 2% of the last three years' profit; projects were sanctioned in Q4. Management called it exceptional and said spreading it monthly would yield about Rs 32-36 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vande Bharat catering model's lower margin change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the licensee fee and turnover both earn margin; the 5% GST on billed turnover, with no ITC credit, is borne by IRCTC on revenue increases.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pending litigation over licence fee for prepaid and postpaid trains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the matter (CC-60 case) is under litigation and declined to quantify or give a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rail Neer capacity and partner status?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambernath and Danapur expansions tendered; partner tie-ups in progress; channel partner talks for the 40% supply gap are ongoing but 'not very encouraging' so far.

qa_highlights.question: Did the August Kranti Rajdhani stop at Agra get considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the route is Mathura-Mumbai via Kota and that a request to Indian Railways would be needed; no commitment was made.

542830|2026-06.headline: IRCTC Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.1% to INR1,370 crore, but EBITDA fell 2.77% to INR386 crore as catering margins and internet ticketing spinoffs weakened.
542830|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 18.1% YoY to INR1,370 crore, led by catering (INR732 crore, +33.8%) and tourism (INR168 crore, +13.5%). EBITDA was INR386 crore (28.17% margin), down 2.77% YoY, and PAT was about INR330 crore. Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. Management said the catering and HR effects are non-recurring and that the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by November.

segments.name: Internet Ticketing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR361 crore (+0.5%); EBIT margin fell to 80.33% from 84.12%, attributed to NGET infra refresh, about INR10 crore maintenance booking, and lower marketing/ad and agent income. About 89% of reserved tickets are booked online.

segments.name: Catering
segments.commentary: Revenue INR732 crore (+33.8%); segment margin 9.29% vs 10.42% in FY26. Management attributed the drop to about INR4 crore proof-of-concept cost on six trains and about INR10 crore HR/gratuity charge; catering onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore.

segments.name: Rail Neer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR109 crore (+2.83%); margin about 10% vs 14-15% prior, driven by resin/petroleum cost rise (material cost INR55 crore to INR61 crore) linked to West Asia crisis. Management said profit fell only about INR4 crore overall.

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

guidance_outlook: Management expects catering margins to return to the traditional 10-12% range; proof-of-concept trains to finish by September (2 trains) and November (2 trains).
The one-time HR cost of about INR20 crore (catering INR10 crore) is not expected to recur in Q2.

Rail Neer augmentation: Ambernath from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles/day and Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles/day, targeted for FY27; four new plants (Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi, Bhagalpur) may spill into FY28.
About 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore).
Management aims to bring non-convenience fee back toward INR150 crore over time via iPay, e-wallet loyalty and agent business changes; no quarterly run-rate given.
Active-active disaster recovery planned at Secunderabad, with further investment expected in Q2-Q4.
capex_capacity: Rail Neer installed capacity about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after closure of one plant (from 18.4 lakh); supply about 15.5 lakh bottles/day against higher demand at some stations.
NGET infra refresh: about INR150 crore infused into PRS modernisation; ticketing throughput about 37,000 tickets per minute, targeted to exceed 1 lakh.
E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day in FY27 from 1.05 lakh a year earlier; e-pantry live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100.
Catering services in 81 Vande Bharat trains run by IRCTC; other Vande Bharat catering is outsourced to empanelled licensees via limited tenders.
Payment aggregator (IRCTC Payments Ltd): final RBI application submitted by 4 August 2026 with SAR and MVP; RBI response expected within this financial year; TSP already engaged.
demand_pricing: Average daily tickets 14.58 lakh; Q1 total 13.27 crore (AC 6.92 crore, non-AC 6.35 crore). IRCTC share of railway ticketing rose to 88.92% from 88.78%.
UPI share of tickets 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

Catering revenue bridge: onboard sales INR413 crore (INR301 crore), licence fee from prepaid and other trains INR224 crore (INR192 crore), static units INR33 crore (INR20 crore), e-catering INR22 crore (INR9 crore), election specials INR41 crore (INR5 crore).
Opt-out for catering on prepaid trains estimated at roughly 25-30% (management said unconfirmed); complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals.
Tourism OTA-linked income about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%); internet ticketing about 18% of total revenue excluding convenience fee, 26% including it.
Rail Neer priced at INR14 per bottle; third-party brands visible on non-AC trains and kiosks. Management attributed this to unauthorised vendors filling gaps at non-mandatory stations.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the resignation of Sanjay Jain and assurance on no material discrepancies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a completely personal decision, praised his leadership, and said he will continue supporting from outside. No discrepancies were addressed beyond that assurance.

qa_highlights.question: Why third-party bottled water brands are visible on non-AC trains and kiosks, and Rail Neer's incremental revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail Neer is priced at INR14 per bottle; installed capacity is about 17.77 lakh bottles/day after one plant closed (from 18.4 lakh) against supply of about 15.5 lakh. Gaps at mandatory stations are exploited by unauthorised vendors. Augmentation: Ambernath 2 to 3 lakh and Danapur 1 to 2 lakh bottles/day; four new plants at Prayagraj, Mysore, Ranchi and Bhagalpur, with timelines possibly spilling into FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Catering attachment rates, opt-in/opt-out mix and passenger-experience steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Opt-out for prepaid-train catering is roughly 15-30% (later said 25-30%, unconfirmed). Complaint ratio about 0.0008% of 18 lakh daily meals. E-catering grew to about 1.69 lakh meals/day from 1.05 lakh; e-pantry is live on 50+ trains, targeting about 100. Branded players are at policy-formulation stage.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Tejas rebranding and tourism margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC runs two private Tejas trains; non-fare revenue from naming and wrap rights is a policy-backed lever, with the Tejas naming done for the first time. It was described as a previously dormant revenue stream now being promoted through regional and zonal offices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the catering revenue increase in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Catering revenue rose from INR547 crore to INR732 crore, a delta of about INR185 crore. Onboard sales from prepaid trains rose to INR413 crore from INR301 crore, licence fees from prepaid and other trains to INR224 crore from INR192 crore, static units to INR33 crore from INR20 crore, e-catering to INR22 crore from INR9 crore, and election specials to INR41 crore from INR5 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the payment aggregator licence (IRCTC Payments) and monetisation plans?
qa_highlights.answer: The final RBI application was submitted by the 4 August 2026 deadline, together with the SAR and MVP; RBI response is expected within this financial year, and a TSP is engaged. Current iPay volume is about 2.7 lakh transactions, and expansion would follow once the licence is granted.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of convenience and non-convenience fee, and why the internet ticketing EBIT margin fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Convenience fee rose to INR248 crore from about INR236 crore; non-convenience fee fell to INR113 crore from INR123 crore. Marketing and ad income dipped about INR3 crore (INR14.51 crore to INR11.03 crore), and agent business was restricted. About INR10 crore of maintenance was booked, and NGET infra refresh and active-active DR at Secunderabad are being invested in. EBIT margin was 80.33% vs 84.12%, and management said it normally sits at 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the catering margin decline to 9.29% and the one-time HR cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Proof-of-concept on six trains cost more than INR4 crore. Total HR/gratuity one-time charge was about INR20 crore, of which INR10 crore was booked in catering, covering gratuity (INR20 lakh to INR25 lakh) and post-retirement benefits. Management said this will not recur next quarter, and the proof-of-concept trains will wind down by September (two trains) and November (two trains).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Rail Neer margin decline and how big was the profit impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin fell from about 14-15% to about 10%, mainly due to resin and petroleum cost increases linked to the West Asia crisis; material cost rose from INR55 crore to INR61 crore. Management said overall profit fell by only about INR4 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What share of tourism and internet ticketing revenue comes from OTA partners and other channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Tourism OTA-linked income was about INR21 crore of INR168 crore (12-13%), or 5-7% from online hotels and ticketing alone. Internet ticketing revenue excluding convenience fee is about 18% of total revenue, and about 26% including it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected run rate for non-convenience fee and the UPI share of tickets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a quarterly run-rate and said the figure will not revert to INR110-115 crore. It aims to return toward INR150 crore via iPay, the e-wallet loyalty programme (growing more than 200%) and changes to agent associations. UPI share of tickets was 51.22% vs 48.72% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat catering model and steady-state margin given the GST treatment on prepaid trains?
qa_highlights.answer: IRCTC's model is largely licensing. Vande Bharat catering is outsourced via limited tenders to empanelled licensees, while IRCTC runs catering in 81 Vande Bharat trains. On a Vande Bharat basis, the licence fee plus GST earns about INR105 per unit against INR222 paid to licensees, with about INR11 of non-claimable GST. Management said the 10-12% traditional catering margin range is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Visibility on new train additions and their ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains are expected over the next year, with licence fee of about INR6 crore per train (up to INR120 crore). Passenger growth of about 8% year-on-year also supports catering charges. Train additions are a ministry decision.

qa_highlights.question: Why has internet ticketing revenue not grown, and is the convenience fee being raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said convenience fee grew about 4.89% quarter-on-quarter and has historically risen 5-7% a year. The UPI fee of INR10-20 is cited as a drag, and credit card and credit line options carry a higher fee of INR15-30. Management said it will push for a higher convenience fee but cannot force a policy decision.

rows.why: Q1 slippages of about Rs.98 Crores (Q4 about Rs.60 Crores) are expected to be largely upgraded in Q2/Q3, and SME yield fell to 9.25% from 9.81% QoQ, so NIM and asset quality recovery depends on this.

rows.label: Fee income recovery to 16-17% of total income
rows.why: Q1 other income was about 15% of income and treasury profit fell to Rs.12 Crores from Rs.53 Crores YoY; management expects insurance and gold fees to pick up from Q2.

rows.label: Repledger LAS run-off complete
rows.why: Repledger LAS book fell from over Rs.2,100 Crores to about Rs.60 Crores and will run off by next quarter under RBI discontinuation from 1 April 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on YoY growth and FY27 NIM/ROA guidance and called Q1 the worst-case margin quarter, but defensive on the QoQ dip in NIM, ROA and other income; analysts pushed on ROA below the 1.3% floor, slippages, and the bulk-deposit cost drag.

542867|2026-09.headline: CSB Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 22% QoQ to Rs.183 Cr, with NIM up to 3.81% and ROA to 1.29%.
542867|2026-09.overview: CSB Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs.183 Cr, up 22% QoQ and 14% YoY, with net interest income of Rs.510 Cr (up 7% QoQ, 20% YoY). NIM widened to 3.81% from 3.66% in Q1, driven by a higher yield on advances (10.92%) and stable cost of funds. Fee income rebounded 20% QoQ, though overall fee income was down about 22% YoY due to market-linked non-core lines. Asset quality improved on GNPA (1.58%) and NNPA (0.33%), with credit cost at 24 bps, though elevated write-offs of fully provided card and unsecured book were flagged. Management said it is entering a "scale phase" with retail liability build-out, SME growth restarting, and guidance of ROA 1.5% to 1.8% next year.

financial_highlights.change: +20% QoQ; ex-treasury +27% QoQ; fee income -22% YoY
vs 3.66% in Q1 FY27 and 3.81% in Q2 FY26
Yield on advances 10.92% vs 10.65% in Q1
PCR 87.65% (79.19% without PWO); credit cost 24 bps

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book grew 36% YoY, but tonnage fell about 6% YoY and disbursements slowed; management targets gold at about 50% of loan mix by year-end (53% last year, 54% last quarter), with a 32% glide path by 2030. Gold yields rose about 50 bps QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate / wholesale
segments.commentary: Corporate segment grew 44% YoY; wholesale split roughly equally across corporate banking, mid-market and FIs, with corporate and mid-market growing faster.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: SME growth remained flattish after exits and customer losses on pricing; management expects SME growth to resume from this quarter after portfolio issues were corrected.

segments.name: Retail (ex-gold)
segments.commentary: Retail growth was muted; the bank degrew loan against security (repledge gold loans, now almost zero) and is keeping unsecured cards, agri and MFI cautious, with unsecured retail to restart around FY2028.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Core fee grew about 27% YoY and is just short of 15% of total income; overall fee is just short of 17% of total income (vs 23% last year, which included one-offs). Non-core lines (PSLC, treasury) declined.

guidance_outlook: ROA this year expected between 1.30% and 1.5%; next year (FY28) targeted at 1.5% to 1.8%, closer to 1.5% initially.
NIM guided at around 3.75% to 3.8% this year; around 3.75% next year.
Cost of funds to be brought down from 6.55% to about 6% next financial year.
Fee to total income assumed at 17% to 18%; IRDAI corporate agency draft may cut this by 0.5% to 1%.
Balance sheet growth guided at 30% to 50% faster than the system; system growth was faster this quarter due to FCNR inflows.
CASA to grow faster than term deposits from FY2028, after being slower this year.
Gold loans to fall to about 50% of mix by year-end; SBS 2030 targets continue.
capex_capacity: Network of 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at September 2026.
Core system upgrade and DC-DR switch completed; OFSAA implementation under way.
Technology investments span transaction banking (supply chain, CMS, trade), OBDX, corporate net banking and corporate LOS.
Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition the current focus.
Opex up about 11% QoQ and about 3% YoY; other opex up 18% QoQ mainly on technology, plus distribution and infrastructure; staff cost up about 17% YoY.
demand_pricing: Gold disbursements fell as rebooking is no longer shown as new disbursement and gold prices dipped; management says the regulator's LTV cut from 90% to 75% was managed.
Gold loan LTV about 75% vs 60-65% at peers, attributed to a larger agri portfolio where higher LTV is allowed; about 28% of gold book is above Rs.20 lakh ticket size.
Gold yields raised by about 50 bps QoQ, leveraging distribution and competitor pricing.
Lost some SME customers on pricing; exited a list of customers after quality review.
Deposit mix about 48% retail and 52% wholesale; FCY, CDs and borrowings remain significant funding sources.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other opex rise 18% QoQ and is it linked to higher other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total opex rose about 11% QoQ and 3% YoY; the rise was mainly technology, plus distribution expansion and infrastructure spends. Staff cost was up about 17% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in yield on advances and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Better asset quality, careful yield management in wholesale and SME, and a gold yield increase of about 50 bps QoQ, helped by distribution reach and competitor pricing. Cost of funds was flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why were write-offs high while credit cost was low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wrote off a fully provided vintage of credit card and unsecured loans with low recovery prospects and no PSL benefit; it said this had no impact on credit cost, which was 24 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI corporate agency consultation paper on fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, so guidance may drop from 18% to 17% short term, with the bank aiming to recover through core fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet growth outlook and retail deposit traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated growth 30% to 50% faster than system; retail current account acquisition has started, and liability franchise takes two to three years to build. Asset growth is not the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is Fairfax or IDBI relevant to CSB, and is there a Fairfax deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fairfax has no deposits with the bank and the board has not discussed the Fairfax/IDBI matter; the transaction is still incomplete.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROA and NIM outlooks for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of 1.30-1.5% this year, 1.5-1.8% next year; NIM around 3.75-3.8%, with cost of funds targeted at about 6% next year to offset mix shift.

risks_watch: Gold loan tonnage down about 6% YoY and gold disbursements slowing; gold book mix must fall to about 50%.
Regulatory fee risk from IRDAI corporate agency draft; fee-to-income could fall 0.5-1%.
Asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm; management points to a declining non-gold SMA book.
Cost of funds at 6.55% and reliance on FCY borrowings, CDs and bulk deposits; CASA ratio slipped to 18.96%.
Opex growth (other opex +18% QoQ) and cost-to-income at 64.8% against the fee and NIM outlook.
Interpretation risk on write-offs: elevated write-offs of fully provided book alongside PCR rising to 87.65%.
542867|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on earnings momentum, ROA and the scale phase, but guarded on the timing of retail growth, CASA recovery and the fee impact from the IRDAI draft. Management declined to elaborate on the other income breakup and deflected the Fairfax/IDBI question as not yet relevant.
key_quotes: Overall, we had a fairly good quarter.

We will start seeing the growth on the SME side from this quarter onwards because most of the portfolio-related issues we faced in SME book for the last one-and-a-half years have been by and large corrected now.
I would say that we would aim to bring down the cost of funds to somewhere around 6% next financial year, which will give us a 50-basis points lift.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 3.81% in Q2 FY27 vs 3.66% in Q1, guided at ~3.75-3.8% this year and ~3.75% next year, with cost of funds targeted down from 6.55% to ~6% in FY28 but gold yields up ~50 bps QoQ offsetting mix shift; NIM is guided to hold rather than expand further.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network stands at 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at Sep 2026 with no new branch additions guided; growth is coming from balance sheet and liability products rather than new physical capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gross advances up 22% YoY and deposits up 18% YoY, with balance sheet guided at 30-50% faster than system; but gold tonnage is down ~6% YoY and SME growth is flattish, so volume growth is concentrated in corporate (+44% YoY) and gold value rather than broad-based.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation metric is disclosed and tech spend is ongoing (core upgrade done, OFSAA under way), but no new capex or branch plan has been announced; a capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 ROA guidance was narrowed to 1.30-1.50%, i.e. effectively a cut from prior implied range, and fee-to-income may fall 0.5-1% from IRDAI draft, so upward revisions look unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 ROA is guided 1.30-1.50% after a cut, fee-to-income could drop from 18% to 17% under the IRDAI corporate agency draft (0.5-1% drag), and cost-to-income is 64.8% with other opex up 18% QoQ.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition already started, though unsecured retail (cards, agri, MFI) is only set to restart around FY2028.

rows.label: CASA growth turns faster than term deposits from FY28
rows.why: CASA ratio slipped to 18.96% and CASA grows slower than TDs this year, with management saying FY27 is the last year of that gap and cost of funds targeted at ~6% from 6.55%.

rows.label: SME growth restarts after portfolio clean-up
rows.why: SME growth was flattish after exits and pricing-driven customer losses; management expects it to resume from this quarter, but the asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm.

rows.label: IRDAI corporate agency draft fee impact
rows.why: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, which would move guidance from 18% to about 17%.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM, ROA trajectory and the scale phase, but cautious on gold tonnage, retail growth timing, CASA recovery and the IRDAI fee draft; analysts pushed on write-offs, other opex and the Fairfax/IDBI matter, which management deflected.

542904|2026-03.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q4FY26: Q4 PAT annualised to ROA 2.1%, but FY27 guidance of ~1.6% ROA, ~25% advances growth and 1.4-1.5% credit cost.
542904|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 showed strong operating momentum: NII rose 26.4% YoY to INR1,092 crores, NIM improved to 8.5%, disbursements hit a record INR9,811 crores, and gross loan book reached INR40,655 crores (+26.6% YoY). Exit-quarter PAT was INR282 crores (ROA 2.1%, ROE 17.2%) versus FY26 PAT of INR693 crores (ROA 1.4%, ROE 10.9%). The RBI returned the bank's application for voluntary transition to a universal bank; management will reapply later with a more diversified portfolio. Management guided to a higher secured mix (about 56% by March 2027), a board-approved equity raise of up to INR2,000 crores in H2FY27, and FY27 ROA of around 1.6%, below the Q4 exit rate.

segments.name: Secured portfolio
segments.commentary: Reached INR20,079 crores (+43.5% YoY, +12.6% QoQ), now 49.4% of gross book. Housing +43.4% YoY and MSME +57.9% YoY; the housing vertical crossed INR10,000 crores.

segments.name: Micro banking
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR20,709 crores (+6.9%); Q4 disbursements a record INR5,245 crores (+11.9% QoQ). FY26 new customer additions 5.4 lakh. Management guides FY27 growth below 10%, a higher single digit.

segments.name: Newer lines (gold, vehicle, agri)
segments.commentary: Grew 292%, 102% and 127% YoY respectively; together about 6% of loan mix versus 3% in FY25. Gold yield is above 14%; micro mortgage yield is 19.7%.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Retail TD plus CASA INR31,955 crores (70% of deposits). CD ratio 89%, LCR 142%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth around 25%: secured about 40% and unsecured about 10%, per the Chief Credit Officer.
FY27 credit cost moderates to 1.4-1.5% of average GLB (exit quarter DuPont credit cost about 1.1%, per the call).
FY27 ROA around 1.6%, base case, with upside possible; NIM guided at around 8.5%, in line with the Q4 exit level.
Opex to ATA 20-30bps above FY26 in FY27 due to investment, then expected to decline; cost to income to stay at FY26 levels.
Secured share about 56% by March 2027. CASA ratio about 29-30% (Head of Retail Liabilities said around 30%).

Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, planned for H2FY27. About 20% branch addition in FY27 (about 140 branches on 776 base). Cost of deposits to benefit about 25-30bps from SA rate cuts; no TD repricing planned.
capex_capacity: Branch network 776 as of March 2026; FY27 plan to add about 20% (about 140 branches, confirmed by management as broadly yes).
Digital, AI and analytics investment on a cloud-led data platform; the spend is driving the opex increase.
Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, to maintain buffer over the Board-mandated 20% CAR threshold and fund growth for about 3 years.
No inorganic acquisition of secured book is planned.
demand_pricing: Industry bank credit grew 16% to INR219 lakh crore and deposits 13.4% to INR268 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026.
Management cut SA rates in April; expects a 25-30bps reduction in SA cost of funds. SA exit cost of funds was 5.21% in March.
No plan to reprice retail or bulk TDs or MFI yields; management is watching competitors who have raised TD rates.
Gold ticket size rose about 60% YoY, with yields up about 30bps QoQ after lowering rates on small tickets.
Management said deposit growth will match credit growth; a slowdown in deposits in the July-August period was deliberate because of excess liquidity.
MFI slippages for Q4 around INR130 crores; Bucket-X collection efficiency 99.8% in March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why does ROA fall from about 2% to 1.6% if NIM, opex and credit cost are flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative on opex and credit cost and covers possible stress in a couple of key products; no specific line item was identified. It will update if the number changes materially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the secured mix shift cut yields and margins, and how much cost-of-funds benefit is left?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30bps of deposit repricing benefit remains. Management cites 2-wheeler, gold (above 14%) and micro mortgage (19.7%) yields to offset lower housing and MSME yields. NIM guided at about 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when CAR is already strong?
qa_highlights.answer: The asset growth guidance is 25% a year against a Board threshold of 20%, and the bank needs growth capital for about 3 years. The raise is planned for H2FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow MFI faster, with a larger share of new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Most FY26 acquired customers are not yet eligible for repeat loans, so growth will be mostly repeat-driven. New-to-bank share is about 25%, possibly rising to 30%, but not 40-45%, which would be too risky.

qa_highlights.question: What is the secured mix target and reapplication timeline for universal bank status?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI gives no ratio. Management expects about 56% secured by March 2027, and the reapplication timeline will be set after a 2-3 year plan, not immediately.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a contingency provision buffer for ECL or universal bank readiness in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No, management has no plan for additional provisions in FY27 beyond the guidance.

risks_watch: ROA guidance of 1.6% sits well below the 2.1% exit rate; management gave no line-item bridge, and the opex investment and mix shift are the main drivers to track.
Secured yield dilution as the mix moves toward housing and MSME; monitor NIM against the 8.5% guide.
Deposit competition: peers have raised TD rates; the bank has no plan to match, so CASA and TD growth need watching.
Micro banking growth held below 10% as repeat-loan-driven; watch the 5.4 lakh new-customer run-rate and any guardrail changes.

West Asia conflict and oil price exposure: management says the book has no FX lending and no oil, gas, defence or aviation exposure, but is tightening 2-wheeler, used vehicle and MSME working capital monitoring.
Equity raise timing (H2FY27) and dilution; universal bank reapplication timeline still undefined.
542904|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and asset quality, but evasive on the bridge from the 2.1% exit ROA to the 1.6% FY27 guide, deferring to opex and credit cost conservatism. Cautious on the universal bank reapplication, which management said will not happen immediately.
key_quotes: Our financial outcome for Q4 reflects near-normal portfolio and operational performance.
The RBI does not share, direct, or guide a particular ratio.
We are being conservative on both our opex and our credit cost.
So we have broadly constructed our secured and unsecured ratio for this year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided at around 8.5%, in line with Q4 exit, so no expansion guided; about 25-30bps SA deposit cost cut benefit remains, but secured mix shift (housing, MSME yields lower) offsets it, and FY27 ROA guided down to ~1.6% from 2.1% exit with opex 20-30bps above FY26's 6.4% ATA.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 140 branches (~20% on 776 base) planned in FY27 and management confirmed it as broadly yes, with digital and cloud data platform spend under way.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances guided at ~25% (secured ~40%, unsecured ~10%) against industry bank credit growth of 16%, with record Q4 disbursements of INR9,811 crores (+32.1% YoY) and gross loan book +26.6% YoY to INR40,655 crores; micro banking held below 10% limits the volume growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Equity raise of up to INR2,000 crores is board-approved and planned for H2FY27 to fund ~25% growth against a 20% CAR threshold, but this is a capital raise rather than a physical capex announcement; no utilisation figure is disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called ROA of ~1.6% a base case with upside possible, and exit-quarter ROA is 2.1% with GNPA at 2.27%, PCR 81%, and Bucket-X collection efficiency 99.8% in March 2026.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guided FY27 credit cost of 1.4-1.5% against FY26 of 2.2%, but Q4 MFI slippages ~INR130 crores and West Asia/oil exposure is being monitored with tighter 2-wheeler, used vehicle and MSME working capital checks; management gave no line-item bridge from 2.1% to 1.6% ROA.

rows.label: Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores in H2FY27
rows.why: Board-approved raise to keep buffer over the 20% CAR threshold against 25% asset growth guidance, funding about 3 years of growth.

rows.label: Universal bank reapplication
rows.why: RBI returned the application; management says reapplication will follow a 2-3 year diversification plan and will not happen immediately.

rows.label: Deposit cost benefit from SA rate cuts
rows.why: SA rates cut in April with a 25-30bps reduction in SA cost of funds expected from SA exit cost of 5.21% in March; no TD repricing planned.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating momentum, record disbursements and asset quality (GNPA 2.27%, PCR 81%), but evasive on the bridge from the 2.1% exit ROA to the 1.6% FY27 guide, deferring to opex and credit cost conservatism; analysts pushed on ROA, equity raise rationale and universal bank tim

542904|2026-06.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR317 crore (ROA 2.2%, ROE 18.2%); FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0%.
542904|2026-06.overview: Gross loans reached INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ) and deposits INR48,129 crore (+25% YoY), with CASA up 37.8% YoY to INR12,930 crore. Net interest income was INR1,186 crore with NIM stable at 8.5%, and GNPA fell 10 bps to 2.17% with PCR at 85%. Management revised FY27 credit cost guidance to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets and raised ROA guidance to 1.8-2.0%, helped by deferred capacity-building spend (about INR250 crore planned for FY27, mostly from June onward) and lower opex (now about 6.4% of average assets).

segments.name: Micro banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Book INR21,371 crore (+16.8% YoY), disbursements INR4,581 crore (+16.4% YoY). Bucket X collection efficiency 99.68%; slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4; provision coverage about 95%.

segments.name: Affordable housing and micro mortgages
segments.commentary: Combined gross book INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). GNPA stable at 1.2% (affordable housing) and 0.6% (micro mortgages). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore, yield about 19.5%, PAR rising from about 1.2% to 1.5%.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book INR21,638 crore (+42.7% YoY, +7.8% QoQ), now 50.4% of loans.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Book INR3,470 crore (+54% YoY); new book GNPA 0.5%; MSME PAR down 13 bps. Ticket sizes rising, with LAP at INR80-90 lakh and working capital at INR1.1-1.2 crore; disbursement yield expected around 10.5%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursements INR467 crore (+183.9% YoY). Sourced from 455 branches (106 added in the quarter); origination LTV 75%, book LTV about 56%.

segments.name: Vehicle loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY), GNPA 1.7%, served through 337 branches with a mid-premium and EV focus. New lines (gold, vehicle, agri) are 7% of the loan book and 9% of Q1 disbursements.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0% (from the earlier guidance), citing opex and credit cost.
FY27 credit cost guidance revised to 0.9-1.0% of average total assets (earlier basis: average gross loan book); credit cost was 0.9% in Q1.
FY27 opex expected at about 6.4% of average assets, lower than earlier plan, as capacity spend (about INR250 crore) is deferred to later quarters.
FY27 planned asset growth of 25% reaffirmed.
Target of 56% secured loan mix by March 2027 maintained.
Bulk deposit ratio to stay around 30%; no immediate further deposit rate hikes seen, with marginal cost-of-funds increase expected.
Opex to decline year-on-year in FY28 as investment intensity eases.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be sustained in affordable housing and non-MFI segments, and is 2% ROA possible on a steady-state basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Affordable housing yield around 12.5% with ticket INR16-20 lakh and about 580-590 branches; some competitive pressure but yields maintained. Micro mortgage yields about 19.5%, and yields do not fall much at INR10-12 lakh tickets.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost of funds rise further, and is any more deposit rate hike needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Brajesh Cherian said no immediate upward revision is needed, only a marginal increase in cost of funds is expected, and this is built into the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance. IBPC, refinance and securitisation are available.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity-building spend and does the guidance embed NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Bala Kamath said about INR250 crore planned, with little spent in Q1 and spend starting in June; the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance includes it. NIM guidance given at the start of the year is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the credit cost guidance cut and are there early warning signs in MFI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Goel said MFI bucket X collection efficiency is 99.7% and July trends are similar; Q1 MFI slippages annualised about 1.72% vs 2.68% in Q4. Each 5-7 bps move in collections would only marginally change credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the micro mortgage PAR and LGD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PAR rose from about 1.2% to about 1.5%; GNPA from about 0.47% to about 0.55%. Management says 18 and 24 MOB vintages have not exceeded about 2.5% and the book is still maturing; bucket X collection is 99.7-99.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How will opex trend after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex is 6.4% of average assets in FY27; Sadananda Kamath said FY28 investment will be lower and opex will improve year-on-year, with exact figures to follow.

capex_capacity: Capacity-building spend planned at about INR250 crore for FY27; per management, little was spent in Q1 and spending started in June (marketing, IT, branch openings), building up over coming quarters.

Branch network at 814 as of June 2026 after 38 new branches in Q1; plan to add 144 branches in FY27 (106 yet to open). Gold loan active branches to rise from about 430-440 to about 575 by end-FY27; gold disbursement exit rate targeted at INR230-250 crore a month by March 2027 (June exit about INR170-175 crore a month).

Affordable housing capacity built at about INR350-375 crore disbursement a month; micro mortgage disbursement about INR100 crore a month, expected to reach INR140-150 crore by March 2027. Incremental book mix tilts toward micro mortgages.
Opex guided at about 6.4% of average assets for FY27; management expects FY28 opex to decline year-on-year as investment intensity eases.

New products: Unsecured Fast Track loan ready to scale after pilot; pre-owned car loans piloted in Karnataka, to test in 2-3 geographies this year; mid-corporate lending started in Q1; purchase invoice discounting added to MSME suite; co-branded credit card in testing. HCV/LCV only after FY27.
demand_pricing: Gross loans INR42,903 crore (+28.9% YoY, +5.5% QoQ); disbursements INR9,245 crore (+41.4% YoY). Secured book INR21,638 crore, 50.4% of loans.

Micro banking book INR21,371 crore (+16.8% YoY), disbursements INR4,581 crore (+16.4% YoY); 1.72 lakh new customers in Q1. Management says demand is rising across almost all states; Kerala deliberately not being grown.
Affordable housing and micro mortgages INR11,210 crore (+40.8% YoY). Micro mortgage book about INR1,800 crore at ~19.5% yield; affordable housing yield about 12.5%, ticket INR16-20 lakh.

MSME book INR3,470 crore (+54% YoY). LAP ticket moved from INR58-60 lakh to INR80-90 lakh; working capital from INR70-80 lakh to INR1.1-1.2 crore. Disbursement yield expected around 10.5% vs earlier 11-11.5%, and below book yield.
Gold loans INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursement INR467 crore; monthly disbursement averaged INR160-170 crore in Q1. Vehicle loans INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY).

Deposits INR48,129 crore (+25% YoY); CASA INR12,930 crore (+37.8% YoY). Bulk deposit ratio about 30%, retail TD now said to be cheaper than bulk TD. Rates raised in June on key buckets; no immediate further hike seen. FCNR(B) raised about INR60 crore in Q1.
Cost of funds 6.86%, continuing to fall. Management sees only marginal increase ahead; no further repricing benefit visible. NIM stable at 8.5%; FY27 NIM guidance unchanged per management.
Competition: management acknowledged competitive pressure in affordable housing and CASA mobilisation and pricing pressure across asset products, but says yields are being held.
risks_watch: Deposit competition and CASA mobilisation: management flagged tight liquidity and deposit pressure; cost of funds may tick up marginally despite no further repricing benefit.

542919|2026-06.headline: Artemis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12.7% to INR 287.32 crore, PAT up 48.3% to INR 31.44 crore, EBITDA margin 21.5%.

Raipur expected to break even in 15-18 months with about INR 20 crore operating loss; direct insurance empanelment expected in 8-10 weeks.
