542920|2026-03.headline: Sumitomo Chemical India posted record FY26 profit: PAT up 7% to INR543 crore on revenue up 3% to INR3,238 crore, EBITDA margin 20.7%.
542920|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult industry year (excess monsoon, regulatory curbs on biologicals and PGRs, West Asia tension), yet the company reported record absolute profit and margins. Q4 revenue rose 1% to INR684 crore with EBITDA up 12% to INR134 crore, helped by a 223 bps gross margin expansion. Management flagged FY27 monsoon risk (IMD forecast 92% of LPA), rupee and input cost pressure, and is passing costs through via repeated price hikes. Board and management succession takes effect 1 September 2026, with Dr. Suresh Ramachandran becoming Managing Director.

financial_highlights.change: gross profit +6% YoY; gross margin +107 bps

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / cash and liquid investments (31 Mar 2026)
financial_highlights.value: INR3,394 crore net worth; ~INR2,113 crore cash and liquid investments

financial_highlights.change: vs 89 days a year ago; receivable days 83 vs 91

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue grew 4% YoY in both Q4 and FY26; branded formulations rose to 81% of domestic sales from 79%. Specialty products are about 30% of domestic revenue; products launched in the last 3 years contribute about 8% of domestic revenue.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue fell 7% in Q4 and 1% for FY26 on shipment timing and softer demand in some markets; branded products are 40% of export revenue. Container constraints (including to Africa) are seen as episodic.

segments.name: Insecticides
segments.commentary: Largest product group at 41% of FY26 revenue; demand was hit by excess monsoon rains in August to October.

segments.name: Herbicides
segments.commentary: Grew 87% YoY in Q4 and 19% for FY26, driven by flumioxazin (soybean), Lentigo (rice) and Mera 71 (glyphosate). No herbicide returns from channel in FY26.

segments.name: Metal phosphates
segments.commentary: Grew 16% in Q4 and 11% for FY26.

segments.name: PGR and biologicals
segments.commentary: PGR decline driven by gibberellic acid after poor grape season; biologicals affected by regulatory approval gaps from about June 2025 to Nov-Dec 2025. Biologicals are 8-10% of revenue.

segments.name: Animal nutrition
segments.commentary: Revenue fell from INR65.3 crore in Q4 FY25 to INR37.5 crore in Q4 FY26. Company is restarting distribution of some products; margin about 4-5%.

segments.name: Custom synthesis (sales to parent)
segments.commentary: Roughly INR100-150 crore annually; management expects FY27 sales of INR110-130 crore, with growth from FY28 onwards.

guidance_outlook: FY27 described as cautiously optimistic; Q1 FY27 looks constructive, while Q2 and H2 depend on monsoon and geopolitics.

Price increases taken on 15 March, 1 April and 1 May 2026, with a further increase considered for 1 June; management expects about 10-15% cost escalation on a large scale, and 20-25% on some products.
Price realisation improved from late March, but management says margin impact could be net neutral or plus or minus a few percentage points.
No incremental revenue from new capex expected in FY27; new Dahej capex (INR150 crore) expected to contribute mainly from FY28-FY29.
Plants running at full capacity, with supply planned on a normal kharif season.
capex_capacity: Dahej INR150 crore project, expected to commercialise in about 2 years; second and further projects to be announced roughly yearly, with each of similar size.
Capex is being executed at Bhavnagar, Tarapur and Dahej; infrastructure progressing well, with commercialisation timelines dependent on parent-company regulatory approvals in export markets.
India elevated by parent SCC to the same tier as Japan, Brazil, North America and Europe for early-stage trials; 2 molecules received for Indian trials.
Management is evaluating high-purity semiconductor chemicals with the parent's ICTM department; an official announcement is expected soon.
Inventory built ahead of kharif: packaging and raw materials held beyond the usual ~90 days because of supply and lead-time risk.
demand_pricing: Management says FY26 agro business grew about 5-6%, almost entirely from volume; pricing was stable for the full year.
IMD forecasts the southwest monsoon at 92% of LPA (below normal); NOAA indicates 82% probability of El Nino during May-July.

Management said agrochemicals are a small share of farmer cost and that fertiliser supply, not agrochemical price, is the main variable for cropping patterns.

qa_highlights.question: Should FY27 margins be seen as flattish or declining, given monsoon, Gulf conflict and cost pressures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are considered sustainable and are being protected through repeated price increases; it cannot control raw material, freight or solvent costs, so it is passing them on as they arise.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory and working capital outlook for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was deliberately built in Q4 because packaging and raw material lead times rose (for example, packaging from 4 days to 8 days); management expects this to protect supply.

qa_highlights.question: Which new molecules could launch in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: TopGrain, a biostimulant from SBC, is registered and expected to launch in the coming kharif; one more product awaits registration and would be launched in FY27 if approved.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Q4 and FY26 growth between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Agro growth of about 5-6% for FY26 was volume-led; pricing was stable for the full year. Q4 herbicide growth was mainly volume, with some channel pre-buying.

542920|2026-09.headline: Sumitomo Chemical India Q2 FY27 revenue fell 2% to INR907 crores and EBITDA margin dropped to 20.5% on drought-hit volumes and inventory cost timing.
542920|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR907 crores, down 2% YoY, with volumes down a high single-digit percentage as a weak monsoon cut consumption. Gross margin fell 240 bps to 40.7% and EBITDA margin fell 297 bps to 20.5% because higher-cost inventory bought in April-June flowed through cost of sales. H1 revenue was INR1,971 crores (down 1%) and net profit rose 5% to INR372 crores including a one-time INR26.9 crore insurance income in Q1. Management said inventory costs normalised by end-Q2 and guided to normal H2 margins, while flagging H2 as challenging due to El Nino and low reservoir levels.

543064|2026-03.headline: Cohance FY26 revenue fell about 13% to INR22.68 billion; management guides Q1 FY27 as the low point, with growth returning in H2 FY27.
543064|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue declined about 13% YoY to INR22.68 billion, with adjusted EBITDA of INR4.77 billion (21% margin) and gross margin of 70.8%. Pharma CDMO was hit by destocking in two large commercial small-molecule products (about INR260 crore impact), API+ fell 8% to INR10.88 billion on shipment delays and the Nacharam formulation disruption (about INR610 million), and Specialty Chemicals fell 2.1% to INR2.913 billion. Management said Q1 FY27 will be weak on revenue and EBITDA, Q2 stable, and growth returning from H2 FY27, with the Middle East-driven freight and input inflation adding 100-150 bps to gross margin pressure in Q1. This was the first call for new Executive Chairman and Group CEO Umang Vohra, who did not give FY27 numeric guidance.

The first new product has four commercial orders for key starting materials, with revenue mostly in Q2 and Q3 FY27; timing for the second is still under discussion.

qa_highlights.answer: Order of weakness is API+ first, then CDMO, then Spec Chem in Q1. Q2 expected stable, with growth from H2 across all three segments as the order book is skewed to H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth be measured YoY or against the FY25 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is measured YoY, but management did not rule out being below FY25 levels given the large commercial molecule lost in FY26; the lag from pipeline to revenue will take time.

543064|2026-06.headline: Cohance Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 23% YoY to INR4,223 million and adjusted EBITDA margin dropped to 2.2%, with management guiding to a Q2 sequential rebound.
543064|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was management's stated lowest quarter ever, driven by shipment phasing in Pharma CDMO (down 38.7% YoY), a weak agrochemicals quarter, low formulation revenue and NJ Bio underperformance. Sapala grew 2.5x YoY and the standalone business delivered a 9.2% adjusted EBITDA margin, but NJ Bio's INR328 million adjusted EBITDA loss weighed on the consolidated numbers. Management guided to sequential improvement in Q2 FY27, YoY growth from H2 FY27, and margin recovery weighted to H2. Adjusted EBITDA of INR92 million and gross margin of 71.5% (vs 73%) reflected negative operating leverage. Management also laid out an integrated nucleic acid business under Dr. P.Y. Reddy with a path to full Sapala ownership by FY30, and disclosed a USFDA Form 483 with five observations at Pashamylaram.

segments.commentary: API performed slightly ahead of internal expectations on favourable pricing and mix. Formulations were below expectations on an API production delay, lower demand for a mature product and a pack configuration change; Nacharam supplies have resumed but remediation continues.

543066|2026-09.overview: SBI Card reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of INR5,141 crore (up 4% YoY) and PAT of INR778 crore (up 75% YoY), driven mainly by lower credit costs. Gross credit cost fell to 5.6% (down 98 bps QoQ and 342 bps YoY) and gross NPA to 1.9%. Total spends grew about 3% YoY to INR1,10,689 crore, with retail spends up 6% to a record INR95,299 crore, and management attributed the weak headline to festive timing shifting into Q3. Management expects receivables to grow from Q3 and retail spend growth of mid-teens to high-teens for FY27, but gave no receivables growth guidance. qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and inventory rise, and when will it reverse?

543212|2026-06.headline: Borosil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR253.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.6% from 17.8% on a ~INR10 crore West Asia cost hit.
543212|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR253.6 crore, with Glassware up 16.8% and Non-glassware up 4.2%, both stated as volume-led. Operating EBITDA fell to INR35.9 crore from INR40.2 crore as fuel and packaging inflation from the West Asia conflict hit margins; management said price increases of 5-7% were taken but realisations lag into Q2 onwards. PBT dropped to INR17.4 crore from INR23.5 crore (last year included a INR7.2 crore one-time stamp duty reversal), and PAT fell to INR12.8 crore from INR17.4 crore. Management reiterated an FY27 EBITDA margin of about 18% excluding other income, and a steady-state ambition of 18% without the conflict impact.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR65.6 crore, up 16.8% YoY from INR56.2 crore; management said growth was entirely volume-led with price pass-through lagging. Utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Non-glassware (small appliances, bottles and flasks, cookware, kitchen essentials)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR98.1 crore, up 4.2% from INR94.2 crore. Hydra (vacuum flasks) remained hit by BIS compliance requirements, offset by domestic appliances and stainless steel cookware.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 18%, excluding other income; management framed 14-15% historically and ~18% as the steady-state level without West Asia impact.

FY27 consolidated depreciation expected at about INR92 crore.

Long-term ROCE aspiration of 20-24% (later referenced as 20-22%) on the business; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Stylenest India (subsidiary) Hydra plant in Rajasthan: 2 double-wall lines commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line expected in Q2 FY27.

Third captive solar plant in Bikaner: 20 MWp with battery energy storage, commissioned in Q1 FY27; solar now meets about 61% of energy requirement. Further 6.5 MWp (Borosil) and 3-4 MWp (Stylenest) solar under evaluation.
Bharuch, Gujarat glassware plant: capex INR42 crore, sanctioned in Q4 FY26 to make jugs, jars and bottles currently sourced (~INR100 crore sales) from BSL Bharuch; commissioning by end Q3 FY27.

Jaipur borosilicate pressware blast furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tons per day plus a third forming line; capex INR50 crore; commissioning by end Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation about 90%; furnace rebuild due Jan 2028.
Opalware utilisation described as full; Glassware about 90%.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 5-7% by category taken across multiple categories (management says some above that); execution started mid-May and realisation lags into Q2.
West Asia conflict net impact on Q1 FY27 about INR10 crore (INR12 crore cited in Q&A), with price increases compensating only a couple of crore.

Fuel cost run-rate: Opalware fuel impact about INR6 crore in Q1, expected to fall to about INR1.5 crore a quarter; borosilicate fuel impact about INR2.5 crore a quarter, expected to fall to INR60-70 lakh. Fuel at 5.8% of sales vs 2.9% a year ago.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate glassware persists despite rupee depreciation and higher freight; anti-dumping investigation pending with authorities, timing uncertain and not included in guidance.
Whiteware (Opalware sub-category) about 10% of Opalware sales vs under 5% last year; management said margins are well below the regular range, so it will not push that mix up.

Omnichannel presence across 24,000+ retail outlets, e-commerce, quick commerce and B2B/export; first two exclusive Borosil brand stores opened in Pune and Gurugram, Jaipur next, capex INR40-50 lakh per store, no store-count target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Glassware's 16.7% growth was price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was entirely volume-led; price pass-through is lagging and was only a couple of crore in Q1 against about INR12 crore West Asia impact. Price hikes range 5-7% by category.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% EBITDA margin for FY27 excluding other income; capex about INR125 crore, with a range up to INR150 crore including solar and furnace maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Has Chinese dumping eased given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says dumping continues with no visible difference despite rupee weakness and higher freight. Anti-dumping investigation is ongoing, and no benefit is assumed in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 growth inflated by channel inventory stocking ahead of price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that view, saying price impact arrives only in Q2 and there was no forced sale or retailer stocking. Inventory build is typical ahead of Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in ~18% margin given historical 14-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that 14-15% is the historical level and ~18% is the steady-state margin without West Asia impact; FY27 target is for 18% on the year, with improvement dependent on price realisation and lower fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to 20-24% ROCE and why is ROCE around 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed low ROCE to heavy capex over three to four years, plus inventory built for BIS challenges. It described 20-24% as a medium-term aspiration; it did not provide a bridge or timeline.

543212|2026-09.headline: Borosil H1 FY27 revenue rose 8.8% to INR 627.4 crore and gross margin expanded 390 bps to 65.2%, helped by price hikes, mix and solar savings.
543212|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 8.8% YoY to INR 627.4 crore, with gross profit up 15.6% to INR 408.9 crore and EBITDA (excluding other income) up 20.5% to INR 107.7 crore. PAT improved to INR 44.7 crore from INR 40.1 crore. Management credited calibrated price increases of roughly 2.5-7% across categories, better mix, operational efficiencies and captive solar savings, partly offset by West Asia-linked input cost inflation. Glassware growth was muted (2.7%) because the Diwali shift moved B2B demand, while non-glassware grew 10.9% and Opalware 7.8%. DGTR issued final findings on 24 September 2026 recommending five-year anti-dumping duty on Chinese borosilicate glassware, pending Ministry of Finance notification.

capex_capacity: Brownfield: over the last two quarters, phased commissioning of more than 20% additional brownfield capacity at Mohali, Nanavati (Mumbai) and Max Smart (Delhi); remaining beds to be operationalised over the next 2-3 months. Gurugram Sector 56 (500 beds): interior and facade works started; commissioning targeted by end of FY27 after slipping from earlier 'middle of second half' guidance, due to labour attrition during state elections, LPG shortage affecting contractor labour (company now serving meals to ~1,100-1,200 workers) and about a couple of months of delay. Initial operations expected at ~200 beds; breakeven targeted within FY28 (Dwarka precedent: 300 beds, started with 140, breakeven in 6 months vs 12-month guidance, H1 EBITDA loss ~INR 35 crore).

Max Lucknow Gomti Nagar: 426 beds currently, rising to 570 beds over the next 2 quarters; further 200-300 beds planned on the 27-acre Gomti Nagar land bank over time. Lucknow Shaheed Path: 700-bed greenfield approved at INR 1,400 crore, phased over ~3 years, expandable to ~900 beds; 5+ acres.

Pipeline (commissioning in next 2-3 years): Max Nagpur 100 beds by FY28; Zirakpur, Mohali 400 beds in FY28; Max Dwarka 260 beds (building plan submission underway, 24 months); Max Vaishali 200 beds (awaiting building plan approvals, 24 months post approval); Max Patparganj 400 beds with D-wall construction started, commissioning by FY29. Dwarka brownfield of 200-plus beds being planned; Dwarka oncology centre to start next month.

Kalinga Hospital (Bhubaneswar, 250 beds, 10-acre site): controlling stake acquired in May 2026, consolidation from Q1 FY27; about INR 10 crore annual EBITDA; plans to revamp and expand. Acquisition consideration not discussed.

FY26 capital deployment: INR 1,627 crore into ongoing expansion projects and facility upgrades at newer units, INR 131 crore for land at Vaishali, INR 146 crore dividend paid; Q4 deployment INR 328 crore.
demand_pricing: Network Q4 occupancy above 75% despite higher operational beds; OBDs up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; ALOS up 9% YoY due to simultaneous multi-location brownfield rollout, expected to tighten over time.

ARPOB INR 77,900 in Q4, after absorbing higher ALOS and discontinuation of select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients (CGHS). Oncology OBDs down ~5-6% YoY; oncology share of in-patient revenue 21% vs 26% in Q4 FY25 and 24% in Q3 FY26. Management expects oncology share to hover at 21-22%, not return to 25-26%.

Chemo-drug discontinuation: discontinued since October 2025; annual chemotherapy billing down ~INR 200 crore (gross); net of GST ~INR 140 crore. Earlier drugs were billed at MRP with ~15-16% margins; CGHS now requires ~30% discount to MRP. Management says this is industry-wide but Max is most affected given oncology and institutional mix. Q4 carries the full impact.

CGHS rate revision: ~INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing; balance INR 30-40 crore (super-specialty rates, at two hospitals so far) to flow over the coming months. Management said CGHS is reconsidering the chemo discount but timing is not fixed. ECHS and PSU patients lack dispensary access to drugs such as Keytruda.

Noida ramp-up: occupancy above 64-65% in Q4 with doctors hired; management says it is in line with expectations. Dwarka at 80-85% occupancy. Management cited a hockey-stick occupancy curve: units break even around 50-55% occupancy, and the real value comes from 60-65% to about 80%.

Other metrics: Max@Home revenue INR 73 crore (+30% YoY, 16 service lines, 15 cities); Max Lab revenue INR 52 crore (+14% YoY, 60+ cities, ~6 lakh patients); international patient revenue INR 227 crore (+12% YoY, 9% of hospital revenue); digital revenue INR 838 crore (~31% of revenue). Q4 doctor costs about INR 435 crore; management expects operating leverage from here.
Management stated the company sees 10-12% PAT margin as the industry's steady state. It said doctor compensation increases in micro-markets are transferred to patients over time.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 26.8% in Q4 FY26 vs 27.2% a year ago and 26.1% in Q3; management expects operating leverage as balance brownfield beds open over next 2 quarters, and ALOS (+9% YoY) is temporary, but CGHS chemo loss (~INR 140 crore net annual) partly offsets.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Brownfield beds (~20% added) with remaining beds opening in next 2-3 months; Lucknow Gomti Nagar 426 to 570 beds in 2 quarters; Kalinga (250 beds) consolidated from Q1 FY27; Gurugram 500 beds (~200 initially) targeted by end FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupied bed days up 8% YoY and 4% QoQ with occupancy above 75%; growth backed by new beds, though oncology OBDs fell 5-6% YoY and oncology share is set at 21-22%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Network occupancy above 75% despite added beds and Board already approved INR 1,400 crore Shaheed Path Lucknow (700 beds); Dwarka brownfield 200+ beds and Vaishali/Dwarka pipeline in planning, so further announcements are probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue guidance raise; oncology share guided to 21-22% (not 25-26%) and chemo billing down ~INR 200 crore gross annually, which caps upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Gurugram commissioning already slipped from mid-H2 FY27 to end-FY27 (about a couple of months delay), and oncology share has been cut to 21-22%; further slippage risk remains with labour and LPG constraints.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Dwarka oncology centre to start next month and other specialties are expected to fill the oncology vacuum; no specific new molecule or product launch quantified.

rows.label: CGHS rate revision balance INR 30-40 crore
rows.why: About INR 100-110 crore annualised already flowing from CGHS rate revision, with INR 30-40 crore super-specialty balance still to come at two hospitals so far.

rows.label: CGHS reconsidering chemo discount
rows.why: Chemo billing down ~INR 200 crore gross (~INR 140 crore net of GST) since Oct 2025; management says CGHS is reconsidering but timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Gurugram Sector 56 breakeven in FY28
rows.why: Dwarka precedent of 300 beds started with 140 and broke even in 6 months; Gurugram starts ~200 beds, with H1 EBITDA loss expected around INR 35 crore at Dwarka-like scale.

tone.note: Management was confident on the brownfield pipeline, Dwarka/Noida ramp-ups and Lucknow expansion, but defensive on the chemo-drug discontinuation (oncology share now 21-22%) and hedged on Gurugram slippage; analysts probed the oncology share drop, doctor costs and capex sequencing.

543220|2026-06.headline: Max Healthcare Q1 FY27 network revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 2,982 crore, while operating EBITDA margin slipped to 24.8% amid new capacity and oncology drug discontinuation.
543220|2026-06.overview: Network gross revenue grew 16% YoY and 12% QoQ to INR 2,982 crore, with operating EBITDA up 15% YoY to INR 704 crore. Margin was flat YoY at 24.8% but down from 26.8% in the trailing quarter, which management attributed to new brownfield commissioning and the Kalinga (Max Bhubaneswar) acquisition. Net debt rose to INR 2,384 crore from INR 1,908 crore in March 2026, and free cash flow conversion was weak as receivables built up. Management guided that oncology normalises from Q3 FY27 and announced a medical education foray.

financial_highlights.change: vs 24.9% Q1 FY26 and 26.8% in Q4 FY26
Average occupancy above 75% on 13% higher bed capacity YoY
vs INR 345 crore Q1 FY26 and INR 387 crore Q4 FY26
vs INR 68 lakh Q1 FY26 and INR 73 lakh Q4 FY26
Q1 FY27; Ashutosh noted operating FCF up only 3%
vs INR 1,908 crore at March 2026; net debt/EBITDA below 1x

segments.name: Max Bhubaneswar (Kalinga, acquired)
segments.commentary: Post-acquisition contribution in Q1 was INR 19 crore revenue and INR 2 crore EBITDA, at 50% occupancy and ARPOB of INR 35,000. Pre-acquisition FY26 revenue was INR 154 crore.

segments.name: Oncology (in-patient)
segments.commentary: Share of in-patient revenue fell to 22% from 26% in Q1 FY26 after discontinuing select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients. Excluding oncology, gross revenue grew 20% and ARPOB grew 9% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Oncology expected to start normalising from Q3 FY27 and be fully normalised from Q4 FY27.
Max Smart's remaining 50% of the 400-bed brownfield tower to be handed over in Q1 FY27 (current quarter); Nanavati's remaining 50 beds also to be operational this quarter.
Management expects Smart and Nanavati EBITDA to ramp within 2-3 quarters of operations; Nanavati Phase 1 to achieve corporate-average margins without waiting for Phase 2.
Kalinga turnaround targeted within about 12 months, with occupancy and ARPOB targeted to rise 50-80%, plus 200-250 new beds.

Insurance: 6% automatic price revision expected at September-October 2026 renewals; CGHS super-specialty rates flowing from June, with INR 140 crore annual CGHS benefit tracking as roughly INR 35 crore per quarter from June.
Medical college plan: about INR 300 crore per 150-seat college, funded through internal accruals, with ROCE above 25-30% indicated; commercial operations expected over the next few years.
Net debt expected to rise marginally by year-end given capex; net debt/EBITDA targeted at 2.5x only if acquisitions are made.

Expansion pipeline: Max Lucknow +100 beds (next two quarters); Sector 56 Gurugram 500 beds phased from end-2026; Nagpur 100 beds and Zirakpur 400 beds in FY28; Pitampura 200 beds in FY29; Patparganj 400 beds by end-FY29; Dwarka 260 beds, Nanavati Phase 2 271 beds and Pune 450 beds by FY30.
capex_capacity: Max Vaishali: board approved INR 425 crore capex for a 202-bed brownfield tower, taking the hospital from 387 beds; construction started and commissioning expected before FY30. Management confirmed this is the same tower previously planned for FY29.
Max Smart: 50% of the 400-bed brownfield tower operational; beds opened are at about 80% occupancy with oncology focus.
Nanavati: remaining 50 beds operational this quarter; Phase 1 beds at about 80% occupancy; Phase 2 (271 beds) to take about 2.5 years and requires shutting about 100 beds.
Network free cash flow INR 397 crore; INR 337 crore invested in ongoing capacity projects and INR 386 crore on acquisitions (Kalinga and Yerawada).
Pune greenfield SPV acquired and now a subsidiary; 450-bed Pune project has IOD and is expected by FY30. Thane and Shaheed Path approvals: 30-36 months delivery after about six months of approvals.
demand_pricing: Occupancy stayed above 75% despite 13% YoY bed capacity growth.
Institutional (CGHS/PSU) share of in-patient revenue fell to 22%, and management said the decline will continue on current infrastructure.
Insurance negotiations ongoing with GIPSA and others; management denied any occupancy impact from insurer pressure on admissions.
Management said CGHS institutional business is loss-making on a fully loaded basis but contributes to fixed costs.
DSO rose to 95 days from 87 days, adding about INR 250 crore of receivables versus Q4 last year, mainly CGHS and PSU collections lumpiness; CGHS new portal is now processing bills.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Parliamentary Standing Committee's healthcare recommendation's impact and any reassessment of expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said the report is focused on affordability and that the company is not reassessing expansion; he said any viability issue could become a consolidation opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Will Max Smart and Nanavati beds drive EBITDA quickly given 80% occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA should start rising by the second or third quarter of operations as ARPOB improves after occupancy ramps; Nanavati Phase 1 is already in that curve.

qa_highlights.question: What are the medical college economics and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated INR 300 crore for a 150-seat college, targeting ROCE above 25-30%, starting at Lucknow and funded fully from internal accruals. PG courses are also planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FCF grow only 3% when EBITDA grew 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yogesh Sareen attributed the gap to a receivables build-up (DSO 95 days vs 87), and a higher effective tax rate. FCF conversion was about 56% against the usual 62-65%; he expects normalisation as the new CGHS portal clears bills.

qa_highlights.question: Will oncology and institutional share recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Oncology is expected to normalise from Q3 FY27 and be fully normalised by Q4. Institutional share is expected to keep falling on present infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex rise materially before Gurugram comes up?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said indirect cost growth came from new capacity at Mohali, Nanavati and Smart plus Bhubaneswar; no major opex increase is expected, so revenue growth should flow to EBITDA.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from new brownfield capacity and Kalinga: EBITDA margin 24.8%, down from 26.8% in Q4 FY26.
Receivables (DSO 95 days) and CGHS collection lumpiness; FCF conversion about 56% vs usual 62-65%.
Kalinga minority shareholder (39% equity, based outside India) litigation over share purchase; company says it has full control.
Net debt up to INR 2,384 crore; management expects it to rise marginally by year-end while capex continues.
Parliamentary Standing Committee's 176th report on affordability and possible FDI caps; no hospital consultations so far.
Insurance renewals in September-October 2026 and whether the 6% automatic price revision holds.
543220|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on capacity ramp-ups, the acquisition playbook and the medical education opportunity. More cautious and deflecting on CGHS economics, receivables and the Kalinga minority shareholder dispute, and it declined to give regional disclosure in the usual form.
key_quotes: We started the financial year with healthy momentum across the Network, recording year-on-year growth of 16% in revenue and 15% in operating EBITDA.
A hospital does not admit a patient, a doctor admits a patient.
We want to avoid giving solo hospital data.
So, one is that oncology will start to normalize from Q3 onwards.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 24.8% vs 26.8% in Q4 FY26; management expects Smart and Nanavati EBITDA to ramp within 2-3 quarters and oncology to normalise from Q3 FY27, and says no major opex rise is expected so revenue growth should flow to EBITDA.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Smart's remaining 50% of the 400-bed tower and Nanavati's remaining 50 beds are operational this quarter, Max Lucknow +100 beds in the next two quarters, and Sector 56 Gurugram 500 beds phase in from end-2026; bed capacity already up 13% YoY.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupied bed days grew 10% YoY with occupancy above 75% on 13% more beds, and new beds at Smart (about 80% occupancy) and Nanavati Phase 1 are ramping.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved INR 425 crore for a 202-bed Max Vaishali tower (hospital from 387 beds), with construction started; utilisation at about 75% and medical college capex of about INR 300 crore per 150 seats also flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin upgrade was given; management guided only to ramp timelines and oncology normalisation, with DSO at 95 days and FCF up only 3% against EBITDA up 15%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Oncology drug discontinuation keeps in-patient oncology share at 22% vs 26%, institutional share keeps falling, and DSO rose to 95 days from 87 (about INR 250 crore receivables build), so FCF and margins may lag until normalisation.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Medical college plan (INR 300 crore per 150 seats, starting Lucknow with PG courses planned) and Max@Home (INR 78 crore, +32% YoY) and Max Lab (INR 58 crore, +20%) are growing service lines, though no firm launch date was given for the college.

rows.label: Kalinga turnaround to 50-80% higher occupancy and ARPOB
rows.why: Kalinga post-acquisition Q1 revenue INR 19 crore and EBITDA INR 2 crore at 50% occupancy and ARPOB INR 35,000; plan adds 200-250 beds, but a 39% minority shareholder dispute is pending.

rows.label: 6% insurance automatic price revision
rows.why: Management expects a 6% automatic price revision at insurance renewals, though GIPSA negotiations are ongoing and insurer pressure on admissions is a risk.

rows.label: CGHS super-specialty rate uplift
rows.why: Run-rate of INR 140 crore a year, tracking about INR 35 crore per quarter from June, though CGHS is loss-making on a fully loaded basis.

tone.note: Management was confident on bed ramp-ups, the 6% insurance price revision and medical education, but deflected on CGHS economics, the DSO rise to 95 days, and the Kalinga minority dispute; analysts pushed on FCF conversion of about 56% and the margin drop to 24.8%.

543223|2026-03.headline: Max India Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 58% YoY to INR72 crores and quarterly loss narrowed to INR6.8 crores from INR35.5 crores.
543223|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR213.4 crores, up 30% from INR164 crores, and the EBITDA loss narrowed to INR83 crores from INR99 crores. Q4 revenue was INR72 crores, up 45% QoQ and 58% YoY, with the consolidated loss at INR6.8 crores versus INR27.8 crores in Q3. Management said the Noida Phase 1 partial occupancy certificate unlocks receivables of over INR150 crores and allows re-filing for Phase 2. Care homes and AGEasy both grew sharply, though care home occupancy averaged lower due to new beds added in Q4. Management is still seeking a fundraise, timing dependent on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: When will Estate 361 Phase 2 launch, and are residential collections lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 launch announcement expected within days as 140 of 180 units are sold; collections are lumpy, with booking fee of INR25 lakh, then 10% on application and another 10%, with construction-linked collections over about 3 quarters, lumpy in FY27 and more regular from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the management fee outlook for E360, E361 and Noida, and the direct cost?
qa_highlights.answer: E360 about INR130 crores and E361 about INR200 crores lifetime management fee; Noida about INR14 crores pending. Variable cost is about 15% of fee; post-completion annuity is about INR10-12 crores per 250-unit community (60% CAM, 40% discretionary).

qa_highlights.question: Will Noida Phase 2 start and how much is pending on Phase 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 sales expected during FY27 after re-approval of building plans; about 440,000 sq ft remaining. Phase 1 construction complete, with INR70-75 crores of pending bills to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: Why no entry into Hyderabad and what is the status of partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Residence entry delayed by unlimited FSI which lets developers maximise density; assisted living in Hyderabad is on the list and to be examined later in FY27. boAt watch product has not taken off as expected, but tech solutions are being worked on; IIT partnership on wheelchairs is a major revenue contributor.

qa_highlights.question: Is AGEasy on track for INR500 crores revenue around FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects continued high growth year-on-year, similar to the past two years, without reiterating the INR500 crore target numerically.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn EBITDA and PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to show path to profitability for one or two verticals in later FY27; labour code and minimum wage revisions are a watch item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of new labour codes and staff costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour code impact is about INR3-4 crores across entities, mainly gratuity provisioning, recognised in FY27 as the code came in March 2026. Payroll is about INR80-90 crores; management said the reported top line excludes SPV sales.

qa_highlights.question: When is the fundraise and what about the INR32 crore tax demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Fundraise timing depends on market sentiment; cash comfortable for 3-6 months, with an update expected this year. The INR32 crore tax demand on Dehradun is being contested via rectification for unallowed brought-forward losses; if accepted, it reduces to nil.

543223|2026-06.headline: Max India Q1 FY27 consol revenue rose 66% YoY to INR68.6 crore, but EBITDA loss widened to INR25 crore; AGEasy breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.
543223|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR68.6 crore versus INR41.3 crore a year ago, though it fell sequentially on lumpy DM fee income. The EBITDA loss was INR25 crore, against INR23.2 crore a year ago and INR6.8 crore in Q4 FY26, because Q4 included an exceptional DM fee. Antara Noida (340 units) received possession offers in June 2026, with about 75% of dues collected by the call date, though revenue recognition is deferred to Q2 on possession. Management said care home occupancy is improving at 5 of 8 homes and AGEasy's ARR is trending up toward INR120-150 crore, and it reiterated AGEasy profitability by around Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +66% YoY vs INR41.3 crore in Q1 FY26; marginally down QoQ on lumpy DM income
vs INR23.2 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR6.8 crore in Q4 FY26
vs INR145 crore in FY25 and INR175 crore in FY24
vs INR139 crore in FY25 and INR57 crore in FY24
1.1x YoY, down INR7 lakh; operations profit INR0.92 crore, 2.3x YoY, 1.2x QoQ
1.3x YoY; down from INR23 crore in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.metric: AACS combined revenue / EBITDA loss (Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27)
financial_highlights.value: INR21 crore, INR32 crore, INR30 crore revenue; EBITDA loss INR14 crore, INR18.5 crore, INR19 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic net revenue (Q1 FY27)

financial_highlights.value: INR22.5 crore in quarter; ITD INR556 crore
financial_highlights.change: ITD collection efficiency 87%; management fee INR47.69 crore till 30 Jun 2026, INR3 crore accrued in Q1

segments.name: Antara Senior Living (residences)
segments.commentary: Dehradun is profitable and fully occupied; Estate 360 Gurgaon is fully sold out. E361 has sold 154 of 360 units by June end, with 27 sold in Q1 and about 34 in July. Noida possession offers went to 340 residents in June, with INR169 crore demanded and about 75% collected.

segments.name: Antara Assisted Care (Care Homes)
segments.commentary: 485 beds across 8 Care Homes in NCR, Bengaluru and Chennai; occupied bed days up 23% QoQ. Occupancy rose at Bannerghatta to 41% (from 37%), Gurugram to 41% (from 33%), Whitefield to 18% (from 8%) and OMR to 12% (from 3%). Four homes reached ARPOB above INR7,000 in June.

segments.name: AGEasy (consumer products)
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR19 crore in Q1, below INR23 crore in Q4 on post-peak moderation. Online gross margin held at 45% (vs 46%). Marketplace ROAS 3.8 and D2C exit ROAS 2.6; marketplace CM2 improved to minus 17% in July from roughly minus 70-80% historically. Monthly revenue run-rate about INR10 crore in July.

segments.name: Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR15.75 lakh in Q1 with negative contribution margin; average revenue per client INR4,000, client satisfaction 96%, sessions rose from 199 to 307 in June. Will be built into residences and Care Homes, not as a standalone business.

guidance_outlook: AGEasy expected to reach contribution and EBITDA breakeven around Q4 FY27 (management: 'by January or last quarter of this year'), with CM2 improving as ROAS rises.
AGEasy revenue doubling target for FY27 (from INR77 crore to about INR150 crore) reiterated; management expects significant Q2-Q4 top-line improvement.
Management said it will report a smaller EBITDA loss next quarter versus the 63% figure cited for FY26 (loss to revenue ratio).

Two new projects, Bangalore (about 300 units, potential sales value about INR900 crore, in final diligence) and Dehradun (under 150 units, sales value INR850-900 crore), are expected to help meet the 1.5 million sq ft / INR1,800 crore annual sales ambition for the year; definitive documents pending.
Care Home expansion decision timed for October-November 2026, subject to occupancy trends; no new beds added at present.
Incremental capital requirement of about USD20 million over the next two years (reduced from about USD25 million), with the second fund raise deferred.
capex_capacity: Antara Noida (340 units): possession offers issued June 2026; residents expected to move in over 30-45 days; Phase II approval is the next step, with rates cited at INR16,000-18,000 per sq ft versus INR7,000-10,000 earlier.
Care Homes: 485 beds across 8 homes; all 8 operational after DLF Phase II Gurgaon relaunch in July 2026; each new bed costs about INR10-12 lakh including operating losses.
Chandigarh project unwound after height clearance denial near flight paths post Operation Sindoor.
Second tranche of preference issue of INR40 crore received in July 2026; management says the total capital need is unchanged but working-capital credit lines are being used to bridge timing.
demand_pricing: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity slowed in April-June amid geopolitical uncertainty but recovered in July (34 units) and August; management says it has not seen DLF's senior-living entry affect sales.
AGEasy ROAS improved to 2.0 at Q1 exit from 1.8 in Q4; conversion rate rose from 2% to 3.5% after brand spend (Anupam Kher as ambassador).
AGEasy repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); management's directional target is 20%+.
Management noted that logistics and China-sourcing disruption raised COGS and forced some airlifting, depressing margins.
Competition: management said real-estate developers and hospital chains can replicate infrastructure but not services IP; DLF's launch plans in Gurgaon are reportedly small and tied to Medanta.

qa_highlights.question: What should change in cost and top line by Q4 FY27 for the EBITDA breakeven target, and what are the Care Home bed-addition plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY27 numbers; breakeven commitment applies to AGEasy, while Care Homes need 8-10 quarters per bed to turn profitable. No new beds are being added now; expansion decision is timed for October-November 2026 subject to occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Blended ARPOB for Care Homes once occupancy rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blended ARPOB should be near INR7,500 as recent bed additions were at higher rates.

qa_highlights.question: Bookkeeping: how much of Noida collections is recognised in Q1, and reconciliation of senior living income?
qa_highlights.answer: No Noida revenue was recognised in June; recognition is tied to possession, expected in Q2. Senior living income includes DM fee (about INR7 crore), Dehradun operations (about INR6 crore), finance lease income from re-leasing (about INR15 crore, treated as exceptional) and treasury income (about INR8 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Will AGEasy's INR77 crore to about INR150 crore revenue doubling plan hold given Q1 revenue of INR18-19 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the plan; July run-rate reached about INR120 crore annualised, with Q2-Q4 expected to show significant top-line improvement as ROAS improves.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 AGEasy revenue was seasonal, and what are repeat rate and CAC/LTV indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited festive (Sep-Oct) and winter seasonality plus marketplace year-end deals. Repeat rate is about 10-12% (88,000-90,000 repeat customers); the directional target is 20%+, and ROAS (marketplace near 4, D2C 2.5) is used as the efficiency metric.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from hospital chains, developers and financial players, and what is the moat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued services and IP, not infrastructure, are the moat; hospitals would dilute margins in Care Homes; for AGEasy, moats are senior-specific products (3 patents granted, 3 filed) and brand. AGEasy market potential seen at about INR1,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Which business gives highest ROCE, and expected cash burn for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: AGEasy expected to have the highest ROCE, followed by Care Homes (about 23-24%+). Management declined to give FY27-28 projections; it said the EBITDA loss ratio fell from 95% to 63% and will fall further next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Capital plan and incremental requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capital need unchanged for two years, reduced from about USD25 million to under USD20 million; incremental requirement about USD20 million. Second fund raise deferred using credit lines; INR40 crore second pref tranche received in July 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DLF's senior living entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DLF's Gurgaon plan is a small addition within an existing township, reportedly tied to Medanta, and has had no visible impact on Gurgaon sales velocity; it welcomes more players for category awareness.

risks_watch: AGEasy breakeven (contribution and EBITDA) targeted around Q4 FY27 / January 2027; marketplace CM2 at minus 17% in July versus historical minus 70-80%.
Care Home occupancy: 5 of 8 homes on model; expansion decision tied to October-November 2026 occupancy trends.
Noida (340 units) possession and Phase II approval; about 25% of INR169 crore dues still outstanding; revenue recognition shifts to Q2 on possession.
Lumpy DM fee and finance lease income drives quarterly volatility in senior living revenue and EBITDA.
Input cost pressure: China-sourced logistics disruption, airlifting, and labour code manpower cost increase.
Competitive entry by DLF (Gurgaon) and other developers or hospital chains in senior living.
Funding: reliance on working-capital credit lines while second fund raise is deferred; Bangalore project's developer reportedly faced financial issues.
key_quotes: So as you can see now, as the revenue is increasing, the EBITDA losses are now coming down.
AGEasy perhaps by January or last quarter of this year will be in that zone.
So we are not building a INR10,000 crores business in AGEasy in the next 5 years.
But the total number of capital required has not changed for the last 2 years.
543223|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and execution-focused on Noida possession, Gurgaon sales recovery and AGEasy ROAS, but evasive on FY27 and FY28 numerical projections and cash burn. Management repeatedly deferred specific guidance beyond AGEasy breakeven and the Care Home expansion timeline.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA loss ratio fell from 95% to 63% and management guided a smaller loss next quarter; AGEasy CM2 improved to minus 17% in July from roughly minus 70-80% historically, with breakeven targeted around January 2027 (Q4 FY27).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bangalore (about 300 units, INR900 crore sales value) and Dehradun (under 150 units, INR850-900 crore) are planned for Q4 FY27 but still in diligence with definitive documents pending; Care Home bed additions are only decided for Oct-Nov 2026 with no new beds added yet, against 485 beds and 41% Bannerghatta occupancy.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AGEasy monthly run-rate about INR10 crore in July (about INR120 crore annualised) versus INR77 crore FY26, Noida possession offers to 340 units with revenue recognition shifting to Q2, and occupied bed days up 23% QoQ.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Care Home expansion decision is timed for Oct-Nov 2026 subject to occupancy; occupancy is only 41% at Bannerghatta and Gurugram, so utilisation is too low to force a near-term capex call and the decision is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the AGEasy doubling to about INR150 crore and breakeven by Q4 FY27 but declined to give FY27-28 numbers, and Q1 AGEasy revenue of INR19 crore is below Q4's INR23 crore, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 consolidated EBITDA loss widened to INR25 crore from INR23.2 crore a year ago, AGEasy revenue fell QoQ to INR19 crore, and doubling needs about INR130 crore in Q2-Q4 against a Q1 pace near INR19 crore a quarter, but the July run-rate of INR10 crore a month offsets part of this.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or brand launch was discussed beyond the existing AGEasy brand campaign and the Antara Integrated Wellness Clinic, which will be folded into residences and Care Homes.

rows.label: Incremental capital need cut to about USD20m and second fund raise deferred
rows.why: Total capital need cut from about USD25m to under USD20m and the INR40 crore second preference tranche was received in July 2026, with working-capital credit lines bridging the timing.

rows.label: Antara Noida possession and collections
rows.why: Possession offers went to 340 units in June 2026 with INR169 crore demanded and about 75% collected, so revenue recognition on possession shifts into Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Care Home occupancy ramp across 8 homes
rows.why: Occupancy rose to 41% at Bannerghatta and Gurugram, 18% at Whitefield and 12% at OMR, with bed days up 23% QoQ and 5 of 8 homes on the model.

tone.note: Management was confident on Noida possession, Gurgaon sales recovery, AGEasy ROAS and the Q4 FY27 breakeven, but evasive on FY27-28 numbers and cash burn; analysts pushed on the Q1 EBITDA loss, the doubling plan given Q1 revenue of INR19 crore, and the DLF entry.

543227|2026-03.headline: Happiest Minds FY26 revenue rose 12.3% in INR to INR2,315 crore (9.2% constant currency) and FY27 guidance of 12.5% CC growth was reconfirmed.
543227|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR604 crore, up 2.8% QoQ and about 11% YoY, with constant-currency growth of only 0.5% QoQ and 6.4% YoY. Management attributed the soft quarter mainly to right-shifted Arttha licence deals and a pause in a large Hi-Tech customer's new product engagement. Full-year constant-currency growth of 9.2% was below the 10% guidance. Management reconfirmed FY27 CC growth guidance of 12.5%, says it is built on a 15% revenue plan, and guides operating margin up about 100 bps to 17.5-18.5% (explicitly not called guidance).

financial_highlights.change: up vs previous year and previous quarter; includes exceptional items
vs 17.3% in FY25; INR401 crore up 12.3%

financial_highlights.value: ~81% in Q4 (vs 77.4% a year ago); above 81% for FY26 (vs 77%)

segments.name: GBS (Generative AI Business Services)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 3.3% of revenue with about 200 dedicated people; management says it is an innovation centre, not a profit-centre, and its margin decline QoQ was questioned. Profitability is captured in PDES and IMSS.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Led FY26 growth alongside Healthcare; management says PureSoftware and Aureus acquisitions are paying off, with strong QoQ and YoY growth.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 12.8% YoY but dipped 5% QoQ in Q4 because a pharma licence revenue element completed in Q3.

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.commentary: Sharp QoQ decline in Q3 and Q4 attributed mainly to one Canada/China-linked customer pausing a new AI-driven automated cooking product after completion.

segments.name: EdTech
segments.commentary: Grew 8.4% QoQ in Q4; Eduweave platform has a couple of customers and several prospects; traction returning in previously challenged accounts.

segments.name: Retail, Travel, Media and Entertainment, Industrial
segments.commentary: Retail/CPG and travel/media delivered steady growth; industrial stable. Retail and CPG cited as having good traction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance of 12.5% reconfirmed by the Board; management is aspirational about 15%. Revenue plan built for 15%, P&L built on 12.5%.
FY27 operating margin to improve about 100 bps to 17.5-18.5%; management says it is not formal guidance and will be achieved while funding AI investment.
FY27 planned headcount of 1,050, with most hiring in the GBS unit and the analytics and AI CoE.
Management will target 90%+ of engineers, testers and service delivery staff trained on and using AI productivity tools by end FY27.
Plans to build a dedicated 1,000-person AI and generative AI team by end FY27.
Will report AI-led services revenue and pricing models (AI-first vs T&M/fixed price) in coming months. Right-shifted Arttha deals targeted to close in Q1 FY27.
FY27 guidance is organic only; any acquisition would be on top of it, and no acquisition is in the pipeline.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 headcount of 1,050; FY26 ended with about 6,500 people, a slight drop YoY, and attrition of 17%.
Utilisation about 81% in Q4 and above 81% for FY26, up from about 77%.

Enterprise AI platform launched recently; Relay Build (agentic SDLC tool, 40% adoption across internal and customer projects) and Agent Hub (guardrails for coding agents) are AI productivity platforms.
Sales headcount to increase in FY27 as open positions filled; hybrid BDMs shifting to client partners and account managers.
New partnerships: Anthropic (early partner, formalised Q4) and UnifyApps (360-degree partnership), in addition to existing Microsoft and AWS ties.
demand_pricing: Q4 pipeline grew 27% QoQ (record), a mix of new and existing business.
Repeat business about 92-94% of revenue; billion-dollar clients rose from 82 to 91 and contribute about 58% of revenue.
FY26 added 51 active customers to reach 306.

Named wins include a US insurance and financial services provider (product engineering), a global warehouse automation leader (engineering and security), and a European healthcare software company (hospital management modernisation).
Warehouse and logistics take-over deal: 3-year, about $12-15 million; a further engineering deal in discussion at about $8-10 million over 3 years.
Southeast Asia insurer account at $10 million-plus, grown 40% YoY with two large new programmes.
Preferred partner for 4 private equity firms, a source of pipeline. Two new BUs under large-account leaders; aim to create 1-2 $20 million accounts in FY27.
Management declined to give TCV/ACV, citing no industry-standard formula; says it is working on it.
Pricing shifting toward outcome-based models as AI changes service offerings.

qa_highlights.question: Beyond the Arttha right-shift, what caused softer Q4 growth, notably the sharp QoQ drop in Hi-Tech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied the Hi-Tech drop largely to one Canada/China-linked customer pausing a newly built AI-driven cooking-hardware product after completion. Healthcare fell 5% QoQ in Q4 after a pharma licence revenue element completed in Q3; EdTech grew 8.4% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the GBS segment margin decline QoQ, and which AI platforms have adoption metrics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GBS is an innovation centre with no separate profitability target; its profit shows up in PDES and IMSS. Relay Build has 40% adoption across internal and customer projects. ELAIRA is an AI companion to ELLIPSE, and SecAIGenie, Eduweave and Insurance-in-a-box are other platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 12.5% FY27 guidance is covered by won deals versus pipeline conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a mix. Plans were built bottom-up by industry groups, IMSS, GBS and CoEs, and stress-tested for H1. The P&L is built on 12.5% against a 15% revenue plan. Repeat business is 92-94%, and multi-year deals give some cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Will sales and AI investments rise in FY27, and what are the margin headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales cost will rise somewhat as open positions are filled and the hybrid BDM model shifts to client partners. AI investment continues. Management says these are not headwinds per se and that margin is still targeted at 17.5-18.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in FY27 revenue acceleration, and which verticals will lead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the pipeline, the 92-94% repeat base, large multi-year deals, PE partnerships, and new large-account BUs under Rohit Mathur (Hi-Tech, industrial, EdTech) and Prathamesh Kulkarni (retail CPG, BFSI, healthcare). It declined to give TCV/ACV for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is any of the 12.5% inorganic, and how is the company different from platform players in AI?
qa_highlights.answer: The 12.5% is entirely organic; acquisitions are integrated and no acquisition is in the pipeline. On differentiation, management cited its separate GBS unit, repeatable solutions, an SDLC CoE for AI productivity tools, and a deliberate delay in building a broad platform until experience was gained.

qa_highlights.question: Succession planning, given promoter holding of about 32%.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said succession planning has been an annual Board-reviewed exercise since 2012, with Hogan assessments added last year, IIM Bangalore and ISB programmes, and some leaders hired externally.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 must close the right-shifted Arttha licence deals to support the 12.5% guidance.
Hi-Tech customer pause could affect revenue if the product launch stalls.
DSO rose to 94 days from 92; management expects recovery via post-quarter collections.
Attrition at 17% and headcount falling to about 6,500 in FY26 against planned 1,050 FY27 hiring.
Margin expansion of about 100 bps depends on utilisation, integration efficiencies and currency, with forward-contract losses noted.
Management has not disclosed TCV/ACV, and the AI-led revenue and AI pricing-model disclosures are still pending.
Sales-team transition and GBS profitability reporting are open questions.
543227|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and the FY27 plan, but more cautious on the quarter, where it explained the miss with specific accounts. It was evasive when pressed on GBS margin and on TCV/ACV, deferring both.
key_quotes: We're putting all our energy and focus into meeting our guided growth of 12.5% in constant currency for the next year.
Efforts are underway to close these right-shifted deals in the first quarter of the current year.
And we've built the plan for 15%, whereas we've kind of -- the revenue plan, but the P&L has been built on 12.5%.
So we don't look at this as really being headwinds. It could be transitory.
Happiest Minds is the only company that has a separate business unit for generative AI.
But at our size of 300 million, it's all about focused execution on the current pipeline and the opportunities, Dipesh.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides operating margin up about 100 bps to 17.5-18.5% from FY26's 17.4%, though explicitly not called guidance, and says it will be achieved while funding AI investment; Q4 margin held at 17.5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines or facilities discussed; growth is via headcount (1,050 planned FY27 hires) into existing delivery capacity, with utilisation at about 81% and FY26 headcount down slightly to about 6,500.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 CC revenue growth guidance of 12.5% reconfirmed against a 15% revenue plan, backed by a record Q4 pipeline up 27% QoQ and 92-94% repeat business, though FY26 CC growth missed the 10% guide at 9.2%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 81% (vs 77.4% a year ago) is in the high zone, but the brief gives no capex plan, land or board approval, and the asset-light model plus 1,050 hiring plan suggests people-led rather than capex-led growth.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 CC growth of 9.2% missed the 10% guide and Q4 CC growth was only 0.5% QoQ, so management has not signalled a raise; the 15% revenue plan is described as aspirational.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 must close the right-shifted Arttha licence deals and the Hi-Tech customer's paused AI cooking product must restart; Q4 CC growth of 6.4% YoY and 0.5% QoQ leave little cushion against 12.5%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is reporting AI-led services revenue and pricing models in coming months, and has launched an Enterprise AI platform with Relay Build (40% adoption) and Agent Hub recently, with a 1,000-person AI team to be built by end FY27.

rows.label: Arttha right-shifted licence deals close in Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management targets closing the right-shifted Arttha deals in Q1 FY27, and these are needed to support the 12.5% FY27 guidance after Q4 CC growth of only 0.5% QoQ.

rows.label: Warehouse logistics take-over and engineering deals
rows.why: A 3-year warehouse and logistics take-over deal of about $12-15 million is named, and a further engineering deal of about $8-10 million over 3 years is in discussion.

rows.label: Shift to outcome-based and AI-first pricing
rows.why: Pricing is shifting toward outcome-based models as AI changes service offerings, but management has not quantified the AI-led revenue or the pricing mix, and says those disclosures are coming in the coming months.

tone.note: Management was confident on the medium-term FY27 plan (12.5% reconfirmed, 15% revenue plan) and the 100 bps margin path, but cautious on Q4 and evasive on GBS margin and TCV/ACV, which it deferred; analysts pressed on the Hi-Tech pause, the Arttha right-shift and GBS profitability.

543227|2026-06.headline: Happiest Minds Q1 FY27 operating revenue rose 14.3% YoY to INR629 crore (6.7% in constant currency); FY27 guidance of 12.5% growth reiterated.
543227|2026-06.overview: Operating revenue reached INR629 crore, up 4% QoQ and 14.3% YoY in rupee terms, with constant-currency growth of 2.6% QoQ and 6.7% YoY. Reported operating margin was about 17.5% despite roughly INR11 crore of forex losses on forward contracts and about INR5 crore of receivables provisions; management says the margin would have been about 19.75% excluding these. Adjusted PAT was INR80.5 crore (12.3% of total income), up 12.9% QoQ and 14.3% YoY, with adjusted EPS of INR5.34. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12.5% and an FY28 aspiration of 15%, but the company needs a pick-up in the next three quarters to hit guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Flat QoQ and YoY; ~19.75% excluding forex loss and receivable provision

financial_highlights.value: about INR80.5 crore (12.3% of total income)

segments.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 22% YoY and 4% QoQ, the fastest-growing vertical in the quarter.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 27% of revenues.

segments.name: EdTech
segments.commentary: 16% of revenues; delivered modest growth and sequential growth, with management saying the vertical has stabilised.

segments.name: High-Tech
segments.commentary: Strong sequential recovery, up about 10% QoQ on a large engagement that began in April.

segments.name: IMSS (Infrastructure Management and Security Services)
segments.commentary: Sequential decline attributed to a one-time licence revenue in Q4 FY26 that did not repeat in Q1.

segments.name: GBS (Generative AI Business Services)
segments.commentary: Around 5.5-6% of revenues per analyst; grew strongly on a small base and showed a sharp rise in segmental margin, which management linked to utilisation and cross-selling.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Americas 57% of revenues; India and APAC grew about 9% and 10% QoQ respectively.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12.5% reiterated (CEO earlier referred to at least 12%); implies roughly 5% CAGR for the remaining three quarters per analyst.
FY28 growth aspiration of 15% unchanged, per management.
Guidance excludes any acquisitions; includes only businesses already acquired.
Two Arttha banking deals slipped: one is being extended and not expected to close as planned, the other is expected to close in Q2.
Annual wage increment falls mainly in Q2 (structures up to C7) with C7-C8 in October; management expects to recover margin through volume and value growth.
Management expects to publish AI-led revenue (across the whole business, not only GBS) by end of Q2 FY27.
Management expects GBS to keep growing well through the year.
capex_capacity: Utilisation 81%, down about 0.4 points QoQ; management says it has picked up within the quarter and is still a focus area.
Headcount about 6,532, net addition of about 32.
Voluntary attrition improved to 15.4% from 17%.
Enterprise AI platform being built as a secure, model-agnostic reusable foundation; more than 100 AI agents and around 60 repeatable use cases.
About 2,000 employees use agentic and AI development tools; engineering teams generate more than 2.5 million lines of code per month with agents.
About 60% of identified infrastructure provisioning scope automated, nearly 2x faster provisioning; AI automation cuts application integration effort by an estimated 80% in covered scope.
AI-in-SDLC COE of about 40 mid-to-senior people; sales team being split into new-business BDMs and account managers.
demand_pricing: Demand described as mixed with discretionary spend selective; clients are funding AI and innovation by cutting run-cost in support, maintenance and infrastructure.
Pipeline grew both sequentially and strongly YoY; deal sizes in the pipeline are increasing; management says the pipeline has a mix of mid-to-large deals.
Two large deals closed (one in Q1, one in early Q2 expected to reach three-digit crore TCV); a few more mid-to-large deals need conversion to start revenue in Q3 and Q4.
Company does not disclose TCV; it is only beginning internal tracking.

Pricing: management says there is no systemic push by customers for rate cuts; some rate increases achieved, though some renegotiations occur every year. Customers ask for metrics showing AI productivity gains.

Deals are shifting from fixed-bid use cases to pod-based engagements and bundled AI plus digital transformation deals; the company is differentiating execution and contract model (T&M with SLAs/outcomes).
Risks flagged: prolonged war and its effect on inflation, and sentiment shifts in the AI capex cycle.
Management says it is seeing a rise in customer demand for proof of AI productivity gains in pricing; a possible new pricing bucket for outcome-based work is under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: How much visibility exists for the implied ~5% CAGR over the remaining three quarters to reach 12%+ FY27 growth, and does guidance include acquisitions or TCV trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance excludes acquisitions and includes only businesses already acquired. TCV is not disclosed; the company is only beginning internal tracking. Visibility comes from a mix of a few mid-to-large deals to convert for Q3/Q4 revenue, two large deals closed (one in Q1, one early Q2 expected in three digits crore), and expansion at existing customers. Two Arttha deals slipped: one being extended, one expected to close in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are Gen AI BU deals short-cycle or recurring, and what is the steady-state margin for GBS?

Top 5 customers were 30% of revenue vs 33% a year ago; 80 customers exceed USD 1 million annual billing vs 73 in FY26.
Heltar early wins across banking, healthcare, retail, consumer durables and education; Middle East and Latin America opportunities emerging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of nonrecurring revenue, and how much of H1 NRR is recurring versus one-time?

qa_highlights.question: Expected volume growth in coming quarters after the plateau around 45 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a long-term forecast but expects slightly improved volumes in OND as festive and e-commerce communication rises.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and M&A focus; RCS and WhatsApp pricing changes?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12% EBITDA margin target achievable and what is the bridge from 10%?

qa_highlights.question: How much of new-product growth is organic versus acquired, and is any of it one-time?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ILD and the Claro relationship; firewall economics?

Firewall is single-digit % of revenue with 50-60% blended gross margin and some advanced conversions expected in coming quarters.

543230|2026-03.headline: Advait Energy Transitions Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR228 crore and PAT 55% to INR19.96 crore; order book hit a record INR1,304 crore.

For FY26, revenue was INR714.52 crore (up 80%), EBITDA INR83.78 crore (margin 11.73% vs 12.87%) and PAT INR58.08 crore (up 75%). The order book reached INR1,304 crore (up 159%), 64% power transmission solutions and 36% new and renewable energy. Management guided to 40%-plus revenue growth in FY27 and a dividend of INR2 per share was recommended. Standalone figures were also read out, with FY26 standalone revenue of INR448 crore and PAT of INR46 crore.

segments.commentary: Accounts for 36% of the order book and about 25%-27% of FY26 revenue per management. Commissioned 75 MW of Adani's solar project at Khavda and has about 67.5 MW under execution there, due Q1 FY27. BESS EPC revenue of INR43 crore (reported as Q4 revenue of INR46 crore) came via group company Advait Green Energy.

segments.name: BESS and electrolysers (manufacturing build-out)
segments.commentary: Dholera multi-integrated facility is expected to be operational in Phase 1 by Q4 FY27, with 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser Phase 1 capacity. Management guided INR100-200 crore BESS manufacturing business in FY27 as the plant starts only around September-October 2026.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 40%-plus in FY27, described as conservative by management; it said FY26 growth was about 80%.
FY27 order book targeted at INR1,600-1,650 crore by end of FY27 against an order pipeline of about INR2,000 crore.
Segment mix shifting by about 10 percentage points a year; FY27 targeted at roughly 65:35 (PTS:NRE).
Margin improvement of about 1 percentage point expected in FY27; electrolyser margins 5%-10% initially, rising to about 20% in the subsequent year.
FY27 total capex of INR300-350 crore, including about INR137 crore for PTS/IPP and INR75 crore for BESS and electrolyser subsidiaries; FY26 PTS capex about INR100 crore funded internally.
Fuel cell: technology transfer with AVL and TECO for a plant in Ahmedabad; manual plant in about 1.5 years, automatic in 2-3 years; management sees about 500 MW of fuel cell demand within 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Solar EPC physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year, per management, with QRs now in place for large tenders.
Dholera facility: Phase 1 expected operational by Q4 FY27, covering 2.5 GWh BESS and 100 MW electrolyser capacity; BESS plant to be 5 GWh over time.
Electrolyser module range: 250 kW, 500 kW, 1 MW, 2.5 MW and 5 MW single-stack, designed for a 100 MW project.
NABL accreditation received for the existing OPGW, ERS and stringing tools manufacturing facility.
Management expects BESS plant utilisation of 80%-85% in about a year and a half from start.
demand_pricing: Order execution timelines are typically 6 to 18 months depending on business type.

Largest-ever stringing tools and capital tools order of INR22 crore in Q4; ERS supply for MNRE of INR70 crore; first Uttarakhand EPC order of INR33 crore; GETCO re-conductoring EPC order of about INR27 crore.
Management said cost inflation in metals, fuel and other inputs compressed industry margins; conductor and transformer contracts have price-escalation clauses, but OPGW contracts do not.
New ALMM rules for solar from June 1: management said bids already factor them in, the split of government versus private order flow is about 50:50 to 60:40, and it expects limited cell-price impact.
Management expects fuel cell demand to start in FY26 but deliveries from FY27-28; applications are data-centre backup, ferries and defence.

qa_highlights.question: Why is guidance of 40% growth conservative given the INR1,300 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a little conservative: FY26 growth was about 80% and it expects robust growth in FY27. Order pipeline is about INR2,000 crore, with an FY27-end order book target of INR1,600-1,650 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 BESS revenue INR46 crore if BOO projects will sell electricity?
qa_highlights.answer: The BOO projects were awarded to the group company Advait Green Energy and booked as EPC revenue (INR43 crore). Electricity revenue will sit in SPVs and be consolidated after COD, likely from FY end.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex and margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY27 capex of about INR300-350 crore in total and expects about 1 percentage point of margin improvement in FY27. Electrolyser margins are expected at 5%-10% initially and about 20% in the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass on commodity cost inflation to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Conductor and transformer contracts have pass-through clauses; OPGW contracts do not. Management said it has factored these into its bid numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why were four subsidiaries created, and who holds the other 20% of one of them?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiaries were set up for focused growth, bank facilities and future equity raises, with AGPL for electrolysers and solar EPC, the battery company for BESS and C&I, Akara for carbon and Aura for assets. The 20% holder was not answered on the call and was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company fund capex and what about dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding will use both equity and debt in a mix based on business composition, and equity dilution would happen only if it benefits shareholders. No quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company move to pure-play solar EPC and what is the solar EPC capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to bid on large tenders including module-supply projects and win some orders this year. Physical capacity is about 100-200 MW a year.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow was about INR5.8 crore against PAT of INR58 crore in FY26; management attributed this to working capital build-up from the Q4 revenue surge and gave no timeline for conversion.
Debt-equity rose to 0.46x from 0.23x, and management said further capex will need a mix of equity dilution and debt; no quantum was disclosed.
Margin pressure from metal and fuel cost inflation and from the NRE mix shift; Q4 consolidated EBITDA margin of 12.61% compares with 11.73% for FY26 and 12.87% in FY25.
Electrolyser and fuel cell timelines depend on government policy and market opening; the Dholera facility is due Q4 FY27 and fuel cell deliveries from FY27-28.
Ownership structure of the 80% subsidiary (Advait Carbon) was not clarified on the call.

Some answers were inconsistent: management cited Q4 standalone PAT as rising from INR15 crore to INR10 crore, and the Dholera BESS plant start timeline (Q4 FY27 versus September-October 2026) was not fully reconciled.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the INR 22 crore TECO investment and its status, given TECO's reported bankruptcy filing.

qa_highlights.question: Ind-AS 115 adjusted core revenue and EBITDA, and the gap between NRE revenue of about INR 4 crore and EBIT of INR 7.8 crore?

qa_highlights.question: What is ConsenPro and what is the market opportunity?

543235|2026-09.headline: Angel One Q2 FY27: consolidated PAT up 58.2% YoY to ₹3.35 bn on revenue of ₹14.3 bn (+18.9%); standalone OPM 48.9%.
543235|2026-09.overview: Revenue held broadly flat sequentially despite softer trading after regulatory changes, while profit grew much faster on operating leverage and a larger client funding book. Consolidated operating margin rose to 45.1% from 34.5% a year ago; normalised for IPL spend and ESOP reversals it was 43.8% versus 43.6% in Q1. Management kept the standalone broking-plus-distribution margin guidance at about 45% annually and reported record average funding book (₹74.5 bn) and record credit distribution in September (annualised run rate ₹33 bn). Client additions were about 1.5 mn, up 11.6% QoQ. Management said October F&O industry ADTO was up about 39% month-to-date versus September (as of 14 October) and linked near-term upside to the SEBI closing auction session (CAS) circular.

vs 34.5% a year ago (>1,000 bps); 43.8% normalised vs 43.6% QoQ

segments.name: Broking (direct/assisted)
segments.commentary: Gross broking share fell to ~55% of revenue from ~60% a year ago. Net broking income split is ~75% direct and ~25% AP channel. September average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 mn, up ~12% from August.

segments.name: Market share
segments.commentary: Retail F&O turnover share 22.1% for the quarter, rising to 22.5% in September; cash share moderated. Options premium turnover share 19.7%. Commodities turnover more than doubled YoY with share down to 44% as the market expanded.

segments.name: Lending (MTF/funding)
segments.commentary: Interest income ₹5.1 bn. About 84% of funded clients have exposure below ₹100,000; 82% of closing book is under 30 days old. Lending rate held at 14.99% despite higher RBI-linked borrowing costs. Management said delinquencies remain negligible.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution income ~₹71 crore in the quarter, about 5% of revenue, helped by credit distribution and IPO activity. Management does not disclose the split. Regular plans are about one-third of MF distribution.

segments.name: Wealth (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹160 bn, up 19.1% QoQ. Management said margins will be in line with industry (ultra-HNI industry yields near 0.5%) and that the book is focused on annuity-based assets. Some AUM is in custody and does not earn fees; management called this a very small number.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹6 bn. Management is evaluating a comprehensive play and plans to bring in a new leader; no timeline given.

segments.name: New businesses (drag)
segments.commentary: Cash burn from new businesses at about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, up from 2.5%-3% about six quarters ago.
