SIP registrations up nearly 12% QoQ; management declined to read much into the September decline.
Management sees F&O pricing as right and is not planning to change it; price elasticity exists but trust is a key driver.
Net broking realisation rose partly on commodities mix; per-segment realisations not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 45% margin guidance include IPL spend and how is employee cost so low?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the ~45% annual guidance for broking plus distribution includes all expenses including IPL. Employee cost fell due to attrition and one-time costs in Q1; FY27 employee cost guided at ~₹1,100 crore, flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross client acquisition slower than the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said acquisitions were up 11% vs Q1 and the company is focused on activation and marginal CAC across channels, including AP, performance marketing and organic. Management said it would invest where growth is available at the right price.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP registrations drop in September?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said SIP registration numbers vary month-to-month and can be optical (counting edits); a broader period gives a better read, and management tracks SIP inflows and active SIPs.

qa_highlights.question: How is rising borrowing cost affecting MTF and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said lending rate stays at 14.99% with no change planned; borrowing cost rose marginally after the RBI benchmark hike but is within tolerance, with NIMs not materially affected. Bhavin said blue-chip and good stocks make up over 85% of the MTF book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wealth AUM fee yield and how much is earning fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Shobhit said margins will track industry levels (about 0.5% in ultra-HNI) and most of the book is annuity-based. Amit said assets were acquired through the year, so applying yield to closing AUM overstates revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the drag from new businesses on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the cash burn from new businesses is about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, versus about 2.5%-3% six quarters ago when scale was low.

qa_highlights.question: Will the closing auction session circular help F&O volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said the circular provides clarity and is a tailwind for near-term F&O, and that pricing is working and not under review.

IPL and brand spend, plus AP channel and new business cash burn of 3.5%-4%, weigh on margins.
Insurance commission reset (IRDAI consultation) and US stock pilot are early-stage and not yet material.

543238|2026-03.headline: UTI AMC FY26 standalone normalized PAT fell to Rs 643 crore from Rs 653 crore, while core PAT rose to Rs 460 crore from Rs 447 crore.
543238|2026-03.overview: UTI AMC reported FY26 standalone core income of Rs 1,255 crore (up from Rs 1,180 crore) and normalized core PAT of Rs 460 crore (up from Rs 447 crore). Consolidated normalized PAT fell to Rs 511 crore from Rs 731 crore, and consolidated normalized core PAT fell to Rs 452 crore from Rs 492 crore. Costs rose sharply: consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was up about 14% YoY even after a one-time VRS and family pension charge of about Rs 130 crore taken in Q3. The company declared a Rs 40 per share FY26 dividend and management said it sees the payout trend at about 95% of profits. Management's single stated priority is growth in MF AUM, with cost discipline as the second.

qa_highlights.question: What was the one-off in Q4/FY26 expenses, and how should employee and other expenses be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs 130 crore of VRS and family pension one-off was provided in Q3 FY26, plus about Rs 4 crore for the Labour Code. Analyst noted consolidated Q4 employee cost of Rs 132 crore was still up 14% YoY; management attributed this to variable pay and recruitment across three businesses. FY27 guidance: standalone employee cost Rs 90-95 crore per quarter, consolidated Rs 125-130 crore; other admin expenses +7-8% standalone and about 10% consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: How did customer acquisition go during the March volatility, and what schemes attract first-time SIP investors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no sharp pick-up in new investors in March; SIP stoppages rose seasonally. February new SIP additions were better than the industry. First-time investors mainly choose index funds, often with Rs 1,000-1,500 SIP tickets. New PAN acquisition is now a sales metric, with FY26 target to grow the 7.16 lakh count.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of SEBI's revised norms from 1 April, and what is the yield outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Exit load TER cut by 5 bps, plus some base TER rationalisation; management expects the impact to pass through to intermediaries and sees no effect on AMC yield. Yield may dilute by 1-2 bps in FY27 due to mix shift to ETFs and low-duration debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan to return equity net sales to positive territory?
qa_highlights.answer: Priority is raising SIP book. Management is repositioning sales teams to sell multiple funds across value, GARP and quality growth styles, to reduce pro-cyclicality to performance. Net equity flows were close to zero in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the employee count fall while sales staff grows, and is RM headcount rising further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix is being corrected toward revenue-generating roles. It does not expect RM count to rise much further from about 260 UFCs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international business and SIF launches?
qa_highlights.answer: International AUM is under pressure from foreign outflows and currency weakness; management plans to hold ground and bring institutional clients into alternatives. SIF: at least one fund targeted this year, first product unlikely to be priced above plain-vanilla MF yields; higher yield depends on long-short differentiation.

qa_highlights.question: How should the Rs 4,000-4,500 crore cash and investments be deployed, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no plans for cash build-up or buybacks; cash retained for liquidity and possible M&A. Dividend trend line is roughly 95% payout including Rs 40 per share for FY26. Business described as not capital-intensive.

543238|2026-06.headline: UTI AMC Q1 FY27 standalone core revenue flat YoY at Rs 308 crore, core PAT up 1% YoY to Rs 119 crore; dividend payout held above 95%.

543238|2026-09.headline: UTI AMC Q2 FY27 standalone core PAT rose 31% YoY to Rs 136 crore, while reported PAT fell 14% YoY to Rs 143 crore.
543238|2026-09.overview: UTI AMC reported Q2 FY27 standalone core income of Rs 324 crore (+2% YoY, +5% QoQ) and core PAT of Rs 136 crore (+31% YoY). Consolidated core income was Rs 398 crore and consolidated core PAT Rs 131 crore. Average mutual fund AUM rose to Rs 4.02 lakh crore from Rs 3.93 lakh crore in Q1, with net sales of about Rs 5,720 crore, but equity and hybrid outflows increased, with Flexi-Cap a key drag. Management said several funds were improving on performance, and that SIP AUM was flat QoQ at Rs 45,572 crore. The CEO did not attend the call due to a family emergency.

segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 4.32 lakh crore at 30 Sept 2026, up about 10.97% YoY from Rs 3.89 lakh crore; 24.01% share of NPS industry AUM. 169 new corporates onboarded Apr-Oct 2026.

segments.name: UTI International
segments.commentary: AUM US$1.67 billion (about Rs 16,063 crore) at 30 Sept 2026; clients in more than 30 countries. Revenue flat QoQ; two new fund launches planned by end Q3 or Q4 FY27.

segments.name: UTI Alternatives
segments.commentary: AUM about Rs 4,045 crore, up 52% from Rs 2,669 crore a year earlier. SDOF IV crossed Rs 1,000 crore (Rs 1,131 crore) against a Rs 1,500 crore target plus Rs 500 crore greenshoe.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net outflows rise to about Rs 800 crore in equity and Rs 300 crore in hybrid, and will employee numbers keep falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Flexi-Cap saw large outflows despite some inflows; the fund is now in the first quartile on three-month performance. Two blend-strategy funds are in the top two quartiles. Management guided standalone employee cost at about Rs 95 crore and consolidated at about Rs 130 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is UTI gaining share in new SIP registrations, and how are ticket sizes trending?
qa_highlights.answer: New SIP registration share is close to 4%, with many SIPs staying. Average ticket size is about Rs 3,100, up over time.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q2 AUM growth came from net inflows versus market appreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Average AUM rose by about Rs 10,000 crore, of which about Rs 5,720 crore came from net sales.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise yields and reasons for the sequential yield movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity and hybrid about 73-74 bps, ETF/index about 8 bps, cash/arbitrage 11 bps, fixed income 20-21 bps. Weighted average flat at about 31 bps; marginal change from repricing commissions after the SEBI TER-to-BER change, passed on to intermediaries.

qa_highlights.answer: Two new UTI International fund launches planned by end Q3 or Q4. First SIF launch is the Hybrid Long-Short fund in Q3; product choices will follow demand over one to two years.

543245|2026-03.headline: Gland Pharma Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% to INR17,428 million with a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to 12–13% constant-currency growth.
543245|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue and EBITDA, led by Dalbavancin launch, tender wins, and new CDMO products, with Cenexi back to positive EBITDA (EUR1 million in Q4). Full-year revenue grew 14.5% to INR64,307 million, adjusted EBITDA margin rose 360 bps to 26%, and adjusted PAT margin reached 16%. Base business (ex-Cenexi) EBITDA margin was 41% in Q4 and 38% for FY26. Management guided FY27 consolidated growth of 12–13% at constant currency, excluding any GLP-1 upside, and a 15% CAGR over the next four years.

segments.name: United States
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR9,716 million (+26% YoY); FY26 INR33,181 million (+11%). 31 products launched in FY26, including 5 in Q4; 24 ANDAs filed and 28 approvals received.

segments.name: Europe and other regulated markets
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR794 million; FY26 INR3,249 million (+11%), supported by the integrated business development model.

segments.name: Rest of World
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,468 million (+17%); FY26 INR6,511 million (+7%). Management said Saudi Arabia shipments were paused, hurting Q4 ROW sequentially; ROW is 2–3% of sales.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR670 million; FY26 INR2,672 million.

segments.name: Cenexi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue EUR45 million (+4% YoY); FY26 revenue EUR182 million (+11%), with EBITDA improved by EUR16 million. Profitable in Q3 and Q4 FY26; Q4 EBITDA EUR1 million. Target of mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin by end-FY27 and mid-teen EBITDA medium term.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 12–13% on a constant-currency basis, excluding GLP-1 and FX upside; management cited about USD40–50 million of incremental CDMO growth and about INR650 crore from base business plus about INR150 crore from Cenexi.
Cenexi FY27 revenue target of close to EUR200 million, with most growth expected in FY28; EBITDA target of at least mid-to-high single digit by end of FY27.
Base business EBITDA margin guided at 33–35% for FY27; consolidated EBITDA margin around 25–26%.
Consolidated revenue CAGR of about 15% over the next four years; FY28 guided at around 15%, with a step-up in FY29 (about 19–20%+) as complex products launch.
GLP-1 volumes and approvals excluded from guidance; treated as upside. Partner approvals expected in FY27, with some launches from Q3 FY27.
Tax rate expected to decline as Cenexi profitability improves (FY26 ETR about 29%).
capex_capacity: Capex plan of about INR2,000 crore over the next 3 years on top of about INR300 crore in FY26; about INR500 crore expected in FY27. Investments cover ophthalmic suspension line, blow-fill-seal technology (next year), and CDMO dedicated lines.
GLP-1 cartridge capacity at 140 million units; insulin vial and cartridge fills may occupy 30–40 million units over the next couple of years until GLP-1 ramp-up around 2030.
Two new lines commissioned in Q4 FY26 at the Indian base business, one more to go live next quarter.
Cenexi Fontenay ampoule line adds 30 million ampoule capacity by 2027; replacement line to be put in place this summer (August).
Cenexi utilisation: Fontenay near 100%, Osny solid orals about 90%, two other sites at 50–60%.
Acquired a solar plant in India to reduce power costs.
demand_pricing: Dalbavancin launched in the US and Europe in Feb–Mar 2026 with strong demand; Vizient contract won, and management said there was no channel stuffing in Q4.
Multivitamin (MVI) approval received in April 2026, launch expected in the current quarter, with steady revenue contribution.
Three to four recently launched products plus a GPO contract were said to contribute about USD40 million in FY27.
Increased demand for existing products from competitively priced contract wins, aided by procurement cost programs and economies of scale.
Cenexi: 5–6 products signed with Cenexi's own clientele; 3 MAs signed for Cenexi to act as a releasing entity in Europe.
Cenexi won a large hormonal drug contract in prefilled syringes with a European laboratory.
GLP-1: 8 contracts signed, 6–7 more expected soon; CDMO for liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide; no specific volumes or approvals disclosed.

Raw-material and packaging: solvent delays reported; glass and vial suppliers seeking 5–6% price increases, with a possible 1–2% overall margin impact; logistics cost impact on revenue of 1–2%, shared with partners.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cenexi EBITDA-neutral in FY27 at EUR45 million quarterly revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA for Cenexi by end-FY27, driven by efficiencies and higher-value product mix rather than revenue scale.

qa_highlights.question: Can Cenexi revenue exceed EUR200 million in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said close to EUR200 million is the FY27 target, with most growth in FY28 when the new ampoule line is commercialised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12–13% guidance conservative given FX tailwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is on constant currency; any FX movement is treated as upside. Q4 constant-currency growth and US growth were not disclosed and will be followed up separately.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 140 million unit GLP-1 capacity is contracted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify contracted capacity, which depends on partner projections; announcements would follow partner approvals.

qa_highlights.answer: The new line is a combo vial and cartridge line, with insulin contracts filling it until GLP-1 ramp-up around 2030 (insulin may use 30–40 million units).

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gland acquire Cenexi, and what is its utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Rationale includes European CDMO entry, MA releasing entity, hormone and controlled-substance capabilities; Fontenay near 100%, Osny about 90%, two sites at 50–60%.

Rest of World (Saudi Arabia) shipments paused in Q4, with a recovery hoped for next quarter.

Q4 one-off milestone and profit-share income (9% and 6% of revenue, as per the management reply) may affect the margin quality.

Currency: Q4 constant-currency growth not disclosed; FX gains contributed to other income of INR1,115 million in Q4.

543245|2026-06.headline: Gland Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR18,003 million, adjusted EBITDA margin 28%, PAT up 47% to INR3,170 million.

PAT rose 47% YoY to INR3,170 million but fell versus Q4 FY26, which had a INR508 million forex gain. Management announced a 55-SKU, USD90-100 million potential CDMO supply deal, a China-sourced liposomal in-licence, and a INR2,000 crore capex programme now being executed; Saudi Arabia NUPCO tender delays hit rest-of-world sales.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation guided up about 5% per quarter from roughly 60% to 70-75% exit FY27 on 80,000 t, versus volume of 13,500 t vs 13,000 t YoY (about 4% growth).

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects Q2-Q4 revenue and margin run rate to hold, but says the Chinese dumping may return and the 9-point duty inversion continues, and Middle East supply constraints could ease.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A new 40,000 t oleochemical product starts trial runs in Q2 FY27, though end market is undisclosed and ramp follows stabilisation.

rows.label: Isostearic acid utilisation above 80% in 1-2 years
rows.why: Management expects a possible positive outcome by end FY27 at some cosmetics customers, but qualification in Europe and Japan is slow and the product is only 4% of revenue.

rows.label: Export growth from dimer and Isostearic acid
rows.why: Exports are 7-8% of revenue today, and management cites India-UK and India-EU FTAs and rupee depreciation as tailwinds.

rows.label: 7-8 large customers enquiring about alternative supply
rows.why: Management says 7-8 large customers have asked about diversifying supply, but it declined to commit to long-term fixed-price volume contracts given volatility.

tone.note: Management was confident on the realisation and margin gains and the 70-75% utilisation exit, but cautious on the sustainability of Chinese import conditions and evasive on the new product's end market, pricing magnitude and R&D disclosure.

543252|2026-09.headline: Fairchem Q2 FY27 revenue rose 49.7% YoY to Rs 167 crore at a 10.5% EBITDA margin, helped by lower raw material costs after the crude soybean oil duty cut.
543252|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 167 crore (up 49.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 10.5% and net profit of Rs 10.2 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 343 crore (up 41.4%), EBITDA Rs 35.4 crore at a 10.3% margin, and net profit Rs 21.2 crore. Management attributed gains to better price realisation from lower raw material costs, higher finished product prices, and lower dimer acid imports. Plant utilisation is still low at about 60-65%, and management expects it to improve as raw material availability rises after the crude soybean oil import duty cut from 16.5% to 11%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Raw material and import duty
segments.commentary: Crude soybean oil import duty cut from 16.5% to 11%, versus earlier 27% duty on crude oils that management said made raw material too expensive. Management called the lower duty the new run rate, said some benefit is already in H1 via inventory, and said market prices are starting to soften. It declined to share the raw material mix.

segments.name: Capacity and utilisation
segments.commentary: Utilisation is about 60-65% (CFO: close to 65%). Management targets 5% improvement every quarter but gave no timeline for reaching 85-90%. Management says it has not lost market share.

segments.name: New fatty-acid product
segments.commentary: Small-capacity plant using novel technology, import-substituting with export potential; commissioning has slipped from end-Q2 to Oct-Dec quarter (after Diwali), with start-up hiccups expected. Management said the market is very large if the process succeeds, and a PFAD bypass product from palm oil is already commercialised and is a different product.

segments.name: Exports and pricing
segments.commentary: Realisation Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 vs Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26. Exports to the US are on hold due to high freight costs. Value-added products (linoleic acid, distilled dimer) are expected to earn a 5-10% realisation premium. Chinese dumping has fallen, mainly due to lower Chinese export incentives, with rupee depreciation also helping.

segments.name: Isostearic Acid and cosmetics
segments.commentary: Cosmetics business is expected to be hit in the near term by slowing European demand and high US import duties. Approval cycle took 2.5 years. Management expects long-term recovery since only four players globally make the product, and sees UK as the sole Cargill plant location.

segments.name: Working capital and cash use
segments.commentary: Working capital cycle guided at 90-100 days for domestic sales, longer for exports, around 100 days overall; trade receivables about Rs 100 crore. No near-term expansion plans; capex only if the new product succeeds; land of Rs 12 crore bought from promoter, already in use for operations and workers' colony.

guidance_outlook: Management is cautiously optimistic for the rest of FY27, citing Middle East crisis and global macro uncertainty.
Management expects to lift capacity utilisation as raw material availability improves; it has said it targets 5% production and volume growth every quarter.
Management did not give a quantified utilisation target; it expects 65% utilisation to rise but declined to give a number or timeline for reaching 85-90%.
Management said it would like EBITDA margins of 15-18%, but said it would maintain the current margin level rather than commit to a higher one.
Working capital cycle is expected at around 100 days, with 90-100 days for domestic sales and a longer cycle for exports.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation is about 60-65% (about 65% per CFO), expected to improve with better raw material availability.

Company bought land worth Rs 12 crore from its promoter; the land is already used in operations and for the workers' colony.
Cost-optimisation energy-saving work is reported as complete.
demand_pricing: Realisation rose to Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 from Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26.
Q2 FY27 raw material processed 12,200 tons and sold 12,300 tons; H1 FY27 processed 24,600 tons and sold 25,800 tons. (Figures were restated inconsistently on the call for Q2 sales.)
Chinese dumping has declined, which management attributes mainly to lower Chinese export incentives, with rupee depreciation also helping.
Import duty on crude soybean oil cut from 16.5% to 11%; earlier 27% duty on crude oils had raised raw material costs; management says market prices are starting to soften.

Value-added products (linoleic acid for oilfield drilling, distilled dimer) are expected to carry a 5-10% realisation premium.

qa_highlights.question: What margin benefit will the import duty cut bring, and is the new run rate sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duty cut helps refiners process more soybean oil, improving raw material availability and lowering prices. It called this the new run rate, said market share was not lost, and said some benefit is already in H1 with more expected via softening prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is around 60-65%, and the CFO later put it at close to 65%. It expects 5% improvement every quarter, but gave no target for 85-90%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the realisations and is Chinese dumping coming back?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation was Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27 versus Rs 130/kg in Q1 and Rs 106/kg a year ago. Management said it does not expect China to restart dumping, citing lower export incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new product and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a fatty-acid product using novel technology, with a small plant expected to start in the Oct-Dec quarter after Diwali, with possible hiccups. It is import-substituting with export potential, and management called the market very large if the process succeeds.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins reach 14-15% or higher on a sustainable basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would like to see 15-18% and expects to maintain the current margin, trying to improve it further. It declined to share the raw material mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Isostearic Acid and cosmetics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European cosmetic demand is slowing and the approval cycle took 2.5 years. It expects long-term recovery because only four players make the product, and said there is no need for knee-jerk action.

risks_watch: Reversal of the crude soybean oil duty cut if oil prices fall, which could again cut raw material availability and raise costs; management sees this as unlikely given high inflation.
Possible resumption of Chinese dumping, which management believes is unlikely.
Delay or technical problems in commissioning the new fatty-acid plant, which has already slipped from end-Q2 to Oct-Dec.
US export ramp-up depends on freight rates; European cosmetics demand is slowing.
Working capital cycle around 100 days with receivables of about Rs 100 crore; management said exports will push this higher.
Management declined to disclose raw material mix or the China import duty on edible oils.

rows.why: Realisation rose from Rs 106/kg in Q2 FY26 to Rs 130/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 135/kg in Q2 FY27, and value-added products are expected to earn a 5-10% premium, though market prices are starting to soften.

rows.why: Exports to the US are on hold because of high freight costs, and the call gave no timeline for resumption.

tone.note: Management was confident on the duty cut, Chinese dumping fading and the new product's market size, but cautious and evasive on utilisation targets, raw material mix and US export timing; analysts pressed on margin sustainability (14-15%+), utilisation, and the new product timeline.

543253|2026-03.headline: Mrs. Bectors FY26 revenue crossed INR2,000 crore (+9.1%) but EBITDA grew only 2.5% to INR257.7 crore, with margin at 12.6%.
543253|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 8.9% YoY to INR485.86 crore, with Biscuits up 8.4% and Bakery up 8.5%, and Bakery EBITDA margin at 12.7% (+25 bps). FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,043.6 crore (+9.1%), EBITDA INR257.7 crore (+2.5%, margin 12.6%) and PAT INR140.9 crore (6.9% margin). Management flagged a new cost shock from the West Asia conflict (about 3% cost impact on packaging, palm oil, crude-linked items, labour and logistics), which it says is covered by price increases and Project IMPACT savings. Export incentive (DFIA) remains on hold, and exports stayed in low-single-digit growth in Q4.

segments.name: Biscuits
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 8.4% YoY and FY26 grew 6.7%; management targets low-to-mid-teens growth in FY27. About 65% of biscuit sales come from INR5 and INR10 packs.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, NaturBaked, QSR)
segments.commentary: Q4 grew 8.5% with Navratri shifting into March. FY26 grew 14%. Management guides mid-teens Bakery growth in FY27, with English Oven at high-teens and QSR at low-teens. Premiumisation is about 55-56% for English Oven.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Low-single-digit growth in Q4 and single-digit for FY26, hit by US tariffs (peak 50%) and the West Asia conflict. FY27 target is low-to-mid-teens growth; the Bahrain and Kuwait GCC markets are affected.

segments.name: Frozen / value-added bakery
segments.commentary: Sells raw dough, baked bread and ready sandwiches, partly sourced from third parties. Growing month-on-month on quick commerce in Delhi NCR. NaturBaked targets about INR10 crore ARR.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Biscuits growth guided at low-to-mid-teens; Bakery at mid-teens; exports at low-to-mid-teens.
Price increases and cost efficiency expected to offset about 3% West Asia-related cost inflation, keeping value addition in line in H1 FY27.
EBITDA margin expected to improve QoQ in Q1 and again in Q2 FY27; management says the objective is 'as close as possible to 14%' but did not commit to it.
Management expects to sustain YoY EBITDA margin unless crude moves sharply above USD100; logistics cost impact may show in Q2.
Outlet count to rise by 40,000 (from 310,000-320,000 billed outlets) in FY27. Target 2030: 40-45% weighted availability in North India (currently about 35%) and 900,000-1 million total outlets.
capex_capacity: Kolkata bakery plant commissioned in January 2026, giving entry into East India.
Mumbai bakery plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and is in ramp-up; English Oven Mumbai is the largest opportunity, where management sees room to scale about 3x.
Khopoli bun line commissioned and running; bread line nearing completion, with products to roll out by quarter-end. Utilisation not disclosed.
Indore biscuit plant is now operational, and distribution will expand into Central and part of Western India. Rajpura remains the main North plant.
A Bangalore facility is under consideration. Each plant is planned to produce burger buns and value-added products, including sourdough and frozen dough.
demand_pricing: Competitor INR4.5 pack pricing post GST 2.0 hurt Q3 and Q4 biscuit volumes; management called it an aberration and said one large player is still transitioning to the right coin pricing.
Management expects a tailwind from GST-driven grammage increases and lower MRPs to fade as inflation drives price sensitivity.
Wheat crop was good; the Bakery QSR wheat cost is locked for the year, and biscuit wheat exposure is limited to gluten. Hedging is done selectively for wheat flour, sugar, milk powder and edible oil.
Quick commerce is a growing channel: English Oven holds a high-single-digit share on Q-com in Kolkata; a Valentine's Blinkit collaboration reached over 300,000 households.
US tariffs were cut from their 50% peak, and new US retailer projects have started onboarding. Export incentive (DFIA) restart is still pending with the government.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the current RM and wheat inflation, and can margins be protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Palm oil, crude-linked items and packaging are the main drivers. Total impact is about 3% including labour and logistics, mostly covered by pricing and cost efficiency, with logistics impact still to come.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bakery growth slow to 9% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Navratri moved into March (from April last year), which hit bread demand in North India. Management called it seasonal and said English Oven is still growing at high-teens.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin hold YoY and can it reach 14%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin improvement in Q1 and Q2, and says margin should be maintained YoY unless crude spikes sharply. It stated the objective is to get as close as possible to 14%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export growth outlook and status of the export incentive?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports grew in single digits in FY26 and low single digits in Q4; FY27 target is low-to-mid-teens. The DFIA incentive restart is still pending, and cost and price actions partly offset its loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of INR5 and INR10 packs and is there commodity hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: INR5 and INR10 packs make up about 65% of biscuit sales, in line with the industry. Hedging is selective, and the hedge levels are not disclosed.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and crude-driven inflation in packaging, palm oil, fuel and logistics, with the logistics impact expected in Q2 FY27.
Competitive pricing risk: a large player still transitioning from INR4.5 price points, which could affect volumes or pricing.
Export incentive (DFIA) hold remains unresolved; GCC exports (Bahrain, Kuwait) are impacted.
Khopoli bun line utilisation was not disclosed, and the new Mumbai plant is still ramping up.
Minimum wage hikes in UP and Karnataka add to cost pressure.
543253|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the Biscuits and Bakery growth recovery and FY27 targets, but cautious on margins: management repeatedly qualified its outlook for the uncertain cost environment and declined to quantify utilisation and hedge levels.
key_quotes: We are very confident of touching on the biscuit segment somewhere between low to mid-teens kind of growth in this financial year.
So we should be able to cover up to not impact on our margins negatively on EBITDA margin side and also on the gross margin side.
Yes, it's an aberration.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Mumbai bakery plant commissioned in Q4 FY26 and ramping up, Khopoli bread line due to roll out by quarter-end, and Indore biscuit plant already operational, with FY27 Bakery guided at mid-teens growth and Biscuits at low-to-mid-teens; utilisation was not disclosed, so the size of the step-up is unclear.

rows.why: FY27 guided at low-to-mid-teens Biscuits and mid-teens Bakery growth versus FY26 growth of 6.7% and 14%, backed by new Kolkata, Mumbai, Khopoli and Indore capacity, 40,000 new outlets, and tariff relief for exports; Q4 Biscuits grew 8.4% and Bakery 8.5%.

rows.why: Bangalore facility is under consideration but no date, capex size or approval was given, and utilisation was not disclosed, so a new capex decision cannot be tied to a specific trigger.

rows.why: Management is cautious on margins and did not commit to the 14% EBITDA margin objective, while FY26 EBITDA grew only 2.5% against 9.1% revenue growth.

rows.why: Khopoli bread line is nearing completion with products to roll out by quarter-end, and each plant plans burger buns, sourdough and frozen dough, though no revenue figure was given.

rows.label: Price increases offset West Asia cost inflation
rows.why: Management says price increases and cost efficiency will offset about 3% cost inflation and keep value addition in line in H1 FY27, though logistics impact may show in Q2.

rows.label: Export recovery and DFIA restart
rows.why: FY27 export target is low-to-mid-teens after single-digit FY26 growth, US tariffs were cut from the 50% peak and new US retailer projects are onboarding, but the DFIA incentive restart is still pending with the government and GCC markets are affected.

rows.label: Outlet expansion to 900,000-1 million by 2030
rows.why: Management plans 40,000 new billed outlets in FY27 from 310,000-320,000, and targets 40-45% weighted availability in North India from about 35%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Biscuits and Bakery growth recovery and FY27 targets but cautious on margins, qualifying its outlook for the West Asia cost shock and declining to disclose utilisation or hedge levels; analysts pressed on margin protection and the 14% target.

543253|2026-06.headline: Mrs. Bectors Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores with EBITDA margin at 13.1%, targeting 14% by Q4.
543253|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to INR548.7 crores and 12.9% QoQ, with exports reported as high-double-digit growth. EBITDA rose 23.8% to INR72.1 crores, margin up 80 bps YoY to 13.1%, and PAT rose 25.5% to INR38.8 crores. Management said price increases and Project IMPACT largely offset input cost inflation in Q1, but expects Q2 to be the most challenging quarter for commodity and packaging costs. Full-year guidance is mid-teens revenue growth and a 14% EBITDA margin by Q4, with about 16% targeted by FY30.

segments.name: Biscuits (Cremica)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR325 crores, up 15.7% YoY; domestic biscuit sales grew high-single digits on both price and volume. Management said biscuit EBITDA margin is slightly below company average.

segments.name: Bakery (English Oven, Naturbaked, QSR)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR215 crores, up 17.5% YoY; Naturbaked crossed a monthly revenue run rate of INR1 crore. Bakery EBITDA margin is above company average; B2B/QSR returned to good double-digit growth.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew at high-double-digit rate; volume-led. Export contribution is about 35% of revenue; US contribution is about 23-25% per management, and US is back on growth after tariff-related slowdown.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 58% YoY per management; Kolkata bakery unit (commissioned Q4 FY26) now serving East markets.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth targeted at mid-teens (about 17-19% cited in Q&A context); biscuits low-teens, bakery low-teens, exports close to mid-teens.
EBITDA margin target of 14% in Q4 FY27; Q2 expected to see the sharpest commodity and packaging impact, Q3 fully covered by pricing and cost actions.
Project IMPACT expected to deliver about 0.4-0.5% cost benefit this year.
Medium term: EBITDA closer to 16% (15-16%) by FY30 with revenue target of INR4,000 crores.
Consumer price increases of about 2-2.5% taken during Q1, with the balance of the impact in Q2; Q1 inflation impact about 1.5%.
capex_capacity: Capex this year covering existing and in-progress projects could reach about INR3,400-3,500 crores at current prices, per management; excludes Bangalore.
Bangalore plant: shortlisted location; this year's new investment approx INR200 crores beyond last year's spillover; machine orders still being finalised.
Khopoli (Maharashtra) plant commissioned March 2026, stabilising; Kolkata unit commissioned Q4 FY26 (about INR20 crores).
MP plant opened mainly for exports (closer to port) with fiscal incentive; now starting central-market distribution.
Capex funding: about 60% from internal accruals and 40% borrowings this year.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand healthy across retail and institutional; consumption better than feared at last call.
Competition intense in biscuits, especially Upper North India; company stepped up trade promotion and marketing spend.
Plan to add 40,000 billed outlets above INR200/outlet (about 12-13% increase in billed outlets).
Export orders are month-to-month, not a long order book; management said no restocking benefit in Q1.
Inflation impact about 1-2% over last year; contract manufacturing about 1-1.5% of revenue.
Domestic general trade split roughly 50% Upper North and 50% Rest of India; English Oven revenue about 80% North India, with upcountry and NCR now roughly equal.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic biscuit growth and mix of price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: High-single-digit growth, with both pricing and volume contributing.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 is the toughest quarter for commodity costs; Q3 fully covered by pricing and cost actions; 14% EBITDA targeted by Q4 and about 16% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Is export growth driven by restocking or one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no restocking; growth is from new SKUs (e.g., peanut butter cracker at Walmart) and projects that resumed after US tariff slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight and fuel (plant fuel consumption) plus higher marketing and trade promotion spend.

qa_highlights.question: Excise/export incentives status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government incentives have not yet materialised; importers pay destination duties. New Zealand FTA and UK are emerging markets.

qa_highlights.question: Capex run rate beyond current cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports about INR3,500 crores revenue at current prices, plus Bangalore; more capacity to be added as business grows; funding 60% internal.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 margin pressure from commodity, packaging and freight costs; management expects only partial recovery in Q2.
Escalation of West Asia conflict, vessel availability and freight costs affecting exports.
Intense competition in Upper North biscuits; sustained elevated marketing and trade spend may weigh on margins.
Execution of Bangalore and wider capacity expansion, and funding mix (40% borrowings in FY27).
Management did not disclose domestic biscuit segment margin; delivery of 14% Q4 target depends on pricing pass-through and Project IMPACT.
Reiterated revenue expectations (mid-teens growth) vs Q1 high-teens growth; seasonality cited.
543253|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on Q1 execution and margin trajectory, but cautious on Q2 cost pressure and the West Asia situation. Management was evasive on segment-level margin for domestic biscuits and on export duty/incentive details.
key_quotes: Importantly, the growth was accompanied by margin expansion.
So quarter 2 could be a quarter where we will be able to cover most of it, not entirely, but quarter 3, again, we will be fully covered.
Naturbaked has crossed a monthly revenue rate of INR1 crore.
So over a period of next 3 to 4 years, say, by 2030 financial year, we want to hit EBITDA closer to 16%.

543254|2026-03.headline: Antony Waste FY26 operating revenue rose 9% to Rs.920 crores; Q4 revenue up 14% to Rs.254 crores with EBITDA margin ~22%, order book at record Rs.18,000 crores.

Volumes grew strongly: total MSW managed rose 15% to 5.69 million tons, and Q4 processing volumes jumped 32% to 1.15 million tons. Revenue growth was 9% for the year and 14% in Q4, with EBITDA margin held near 22% for both periods, though reported PAT was Rs.92 crores and Q4 PAT of Rs.37 crores was flattered by a Rs.24 crore one-time income in the prior-year base. Management reiterated 15-20% revenue CAGR over five years, citing the record order book and two large AP WTE projects.

543254|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6% YoY to ₹269 crore, but EBITDA fell 27% to ₹45 crore (16.8% margin) and PAT dropped to ₹0.7 crore after one-offs.
543254|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 6% YoY to ₹269 crore on higher volumes and tariff escalation. EBITDA margin compressed to 16.8% from 24.4% a year ago, driven by higher transport/hiring costs at the CIDCO site, employee costs rising to 34% of revenue, and about ₹10 crore of deferred Q4 FY26 disposal work. The PCMC WtE plant was shut after a July 8 landslide of legacy waste that killed nine people, and management flagged a ₹22-24 crore impairment (before insurance) as an exceptional item. The company also refinanced ₹140 crore of Antony Lara's term loan from 10.25% to 8.25%, with a ₹7 crore prepayment charge.

qa_highlights.answer: MRF and composting restarted July 28 at about 400 tons/day. WtE plant expected back by first/second week of October; fixed cost of ₹2.5-3 crore per month (about ₹7 crore) sits on the books meanwhile. Tipping fees continue, but power generation and sale revenue is hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did processing revenue growth moderate, and what is the margin trajectory from Q2/Q3 given cost inflation and wage hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Slowdown is due to the CIDCO bio-mining contract ending (a two-year project). Atkoli going live by Q4 restores growth. Transport and hiring costs pressured C&T margins; renegotiation with transport vendors should give some respite. Labour DA pressure is timing-related, with relief expected in H2 FY27 via escalations. 543257|2026-03.headline: IRFC FY26 sanctions reached ~INR74,000 crore and disbursements ~INR35,000 crore, with Q4 PAT flat quarter-on-quarter at ~INR1,684 crore.
543257|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue and PAT (crossing INR7,000 crore) and net worth of INR56,000-odd crore, with AUM up to INR4.85 lakh crore on a net basis. Q4 PAT was flat as new RBI-linked provisioning on non-railway (CPSE and state-government) lending and higher CSR spend offset revenue growth of about 9%. The company is diversifying beyond Indian Railways, earning NIMs of 100-120 bps on new assets against about 35-40 bps on railway business. No numeric FY27 guidance was given; management set a benchmark of repeating FY26 sanction and disbursement volumes and targeted double-digit growth in top line, PAT, EPS and NIM.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 PAT fall and why did OCI drop by about INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new provisioning on CPSE and state-government lending, higher CSR spend and lower other income (a tax refund interest item in Q3). OCI reflects mark-to-market on hedged foreign-currency borrowings for non-railway lending, which is temporary under Ind AS 109 cash-flow hedge accounting.

qa_highlights.question: How will IRFC keep zero NPA as it lends to state governments and other entities?
qa_highlights.answer: It lends only to CPSE subsidiaries (NTPC, GAIL, Coal India, IOCL) and to GenCos and TransCos with PPA and cost-plus structures; it avoids DISCOMs and high-consumption southern states. Examples include MAHAGENCO, Chhattisgarh and Haryana.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding strategy and liquidity plan?
qa_highlights.answer: ECB target of 30-35% of the borrowing mix; the company has done yen ECBs of $300 million, $400 million, and has a $1.1 billion yen bid open. Bonds at 5.25% and a zero-coupon bond were issued; 54EC bonds are being targeted.

risks_watch: Q4 PAT was flat QoQ and, per the analyst, fell about INR100 crore; provisioning on non-railway exposure is a new drag to watch.
Rising interest rates and domestic bond costs may pressure margins; management said rates are being revised upward.
Competition for the NTPC/UP JV tender (INR28,000-29,000 crore) and other large RFPs could compress margins from the 100-120 bps target.
Currency and hedging risk on non-railway ECB borrowings; OCI volatility until the hedges reverse.
Whether AUM crosses INR5 lakh crore in H1 FY27 and whether NIM reaches the 1.65% target.
Tax benefit lasts only 5-7 years unless leasing business for rolling stock continues.
Credit quality of state-government and CPSE exposure as the mix shifts away from Indian Railways.

we are zero NPA company. And typically, every forum, I say that zero NPA is not a status symbol for this company but it is a business proposition.

543257|2026-06.headline: IRFC Q1 FY27: disbursement slow at about INR2,000 crore and AUM dipped QoQ, but management reiterates about INR5 lakh crore year-end AUM.
543257|2026-06.overview: Management framed FY27 as a consolidation year, building toward 2030 midterm and 2037 long-term plans after FY26 agreements above INR75,000 crore and disbursements above INR35,000 crore. Q1 disbursement was about INR2,000 crore and AUM declined slightly on an accrual basis, which management attributed to scheduled repayments from railways that fall in September. Management said the company is now a near-record on revenue and PAT, helped by a forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements. The call focused on the "Fund in India" conduit model, high-speed rail and DFC pipeline, NIM targets, and questions on fertiliser exposure and the agreement-to-disbursement lag.

segments.name: Railways (core, sole financier)
segments.commentary: Management says IRFC remains the sole financing arm for Indian Railways; no railway business was booked in FY24 but FY26 saw a restart in diversification. Railway repayments drive quarterly AUM dips.

segments.name: Diversified / non-railway (fertiliser, metro, GenCo, ports)
segments.commentary: Three HURL urea plants (Gorakhpur, Barauni, Sindri) are financed on railway-linkage grounds, refinanced from SBI-led lenders at 50bps+ lower cost. Hyderabad Metro Phase 1 refinancing signed; Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) pending decision.

guidance_outlook: Year-end FY27 AUM targeted around INR5 lakh crore (management: possibly INR4.95 lakh crore); mid-year guidance of about INR5 lakh crore also referenced.
FY27 disbursement guided to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore; Q2-Q4 expected to pick up, with some refinancing assets in the pipeline.
NIM target: about 10bps average annual improvement, 2% by end-2030; FY27 NIM targeted above 1.6%, with Q4 NIM expected to be higher than the 1.65% full-year ambition referenced by the analyst.

demand_pricing: Management says recent open-tender rates for GenCo and transport projects are around 8%, and IRFC is comfortable lending at that level with 100bps+ margin.
Fund in India: IRFC intends to act as a conduit for bilateral and multilateral funding, offering bespoke tenor and currency solutions.
Competitors' NIMs are falling across the sector per management; IRFC's low overhead cost is cited as the advantage.
Q1 disbursement was small because the pipeline is thin; management says it is not reliant on FY26 agreements converting in-year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company hold the INR5 lakh crore AUM guidance at half-year and end FY27, and what is the disbursement and AUM growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about INR5 lakh crore AUM by year-end, noting it may land at INR4.95 lakh crore. FY27 disbursement is expected to exceed FY26's INR35,000 crore. The Q1 AUM dip reflects a September repayment from railways.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow only 2% YoY against AUM growth of about 4%, implying NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM rose from 1.40% in FY25 to 1.50% in FY26 and is expected to exceed 1.6% by year-end. Legacy 35-40bps assets are repaying and being replaced with higher-yield assets, which is a gradual effect over one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the material other income in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A forex gain on yen-denominated funding for metro disbursements, reflecting rupee appreciation against the yen. Management said the gain is accounted per Ind AS and a corresponding metro receipt is expected in Q2. Last year's Q4 saw a INR7 crore forex loss.

qa_highlights.question: How are the fertiliser borrowers linked to railways, and is there sponsor support or guarantee for these loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the HURL urea plants depend on railway sidings for raw material and finished urea movement. Output is sold to government agencies on a cost-plus model with 10-12% margin. Management described the loans as refinancing of an existing SBI-led bank facility, with rate cuts of at least 50bps. No explicit sponsor guarantee was described.

qa_highlights.question: What does the agreements-executed versus disbursement table mean, and why is there a lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR92,799 crore of agreements were largely greenfield, of which about INR37,000 crore has been disbursed. Greenfield funding typically starts 3 to 5 years after agreement, with the remainder expected over 1 to 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on diversification into metro and infrastructure, and are there delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hyderabad Metro is on track, with Phase 1 refinancing signed and Phase 2 (about 125 km, around INR40,000 crore) awaiting a decision. Pipeline spans high-speed rail, DFC, metro, rapid rail, ports, GenCo, transco and renewables linked to railways.

543257|2026-09.headline: IRFC reports H1 FY27 revenue up over 20% and PAT up over 10%; management reiterates ~INR5 lakh crore AUM target for FY27.
543257|2026-09.overview: Management said H1 FY27 beat both company guidance and street expectations, with revenue up more than 20% and PAT up more than 10% year on year. The CEO said PAT grew in double digits in five of the last six quarters, the exception being Q4 FY26, which carried provisions for new business under RBI norms. Diversification beyond the Indian Railways single-client model is the core theme, with non-railway lending at margins 2-3.5 times the railway book. The call also covered a large pipeline of railway-linked financing (DFC, high-speed rail, freight JVs) that management expects to start in FY28. Most Q&A was on strategy and shareholder value; the transcript gives no reported Q2 figures beyond the H1 growth rates.

segments.name: Railways (IR) lending
segments.commentary: Management said about 90% plus of AUM is with Railways, at a NIM of about 1.3% (around 35 bps margin on cost-plus). Railway book is being replaced over time by higher-yield non-IR assets.

segments.name: Non-railway lending (diversification)
segments.commentary: Non-IR assets earn margins of 2-3.5 times the railway book, per management; INR35,000 crore of disbursement last year was non-IR. Pipeline covers metros, ports, renewables, thermal power, Gencos linked to Railways, and some road linkages, targeted for Q3 or early Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements to exceed last year's level; guidance reiterated.
AUM target of near INR5 lakh crore (possibly slightly short by INR1,000-2,000 crore) by end FY27; management expects to show progress by Q3.
PAT expected to grow near 10% annually even with flat AUM, as non-IR assets replace railway assets at higher yields.

Railway-related funding of minimum about INR50,000 crore a year from FY28 for next decade, subject to the funding model (multilateral/aggregator role) to be finalised by end FY27; clearer numbers promised in Q3.
Mix target of 60% pure railways and 40% diversification by 2030.
Margin floor of INR0.85-0.90 per the ALM policy on non-railway loans; WACC target of 6.55% to be maintained.
capex_capacity: Management cited a Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dankuni to Surat (over 2,000 km, more than INR3 lakh crore), seven sanctioned high-speed rail corridors, and six freight lines planned under JV/PPP; total pie over INR20 lakh crore over about 10 years.
IRFC plans to act as sole financing arm and aggregator, with talks under way with the World Bank, other multilaterals and domestic players; model expected in place by end FY27.
Employee headcount roughly doubled in the last year, per the CEO.
demand_pricing: Floating-rate exposure: repo rate up 25 bps and back-to-back TONAR up 25 bps; management says it passes these through on non-railway loans and that resets are both ways.
Yen borrowing: about USD2 billion raised last year at around 1.8%, now about 2.25% after TONAR increases; hedging cost stated as not above 6.3%.
Term loans from banks are about 25% of the borrowing mix; management claims a 20-30 bps cushion against rate moves.
Prepayment: management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no floor on benchmark-linked pricing, and lowest-in-market cost of funds.
Overhead cost cited at about INR0.15 per unit of lending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities, and what are the main risks on railway capex, asset growth or funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 disbursements will exceed FY26, with non-IR pipeline (metros, ports, renewables, thermal, Gencos, roads) ready for Q3 or early Q4. Railway-linked funding is to start from FY28 at a minimum of INR50,000 crore a year, with the aggregator model to be set by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key financial risks (NIM, borrowing costs, asset quality) in a changing rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO cited a 6.55% WACC, lower than other NBFCs, and a push to raise more 54EC bonds and ECB. Management said the ALM team monitors margins weekly and keeps a minimum spread of INR0.85-0.90 on non-railway loans.

qa_highlights.question: How is non-railway lending priced, and how fast can rate increases be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Loans are priced on a cost-plus basis, and floating-rate loans reset monthly, quarterly or yearly. Management said a 25 bps repo hike and TONAR increase were passed through, and the company keeps a 20-30 bps cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there prepayment pressure, as seen at other government lenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no prepayment pressure, citing no prepayment penalty, no benchmark floor, and the cheapest funding in the market. Some prepayments by borrowers into IRFC were said to be business wins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM and disbursement vision, and is the INR5 lakh crore AUM target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated near INR5 lakh crore AUM by end FY27 (possibly 1,000-2,000 crore short), up from INR4.85 lakh crore at end FY26. It targets a 60:40 railway-to-diversified mix by 2030 and near-10% PAT growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the share price move so much, and what are the dividend and value prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said share price moves are outside its control and pointed to fundamentals. It cited an interim dividend of INR1.15 this year against INR1.05 last year, and a payout of about 40% of profit over the last two years.

Rising floating rates (repo and TONAR each up 25 bps) and hardening yen hedge costs could squeeze spreads if pass-through lags.

543258|2026-03.headline: Indigo Paints Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 8.4% to INR397.9 crore; management signals margin sacrifice of 2-2.5pp to chase faster top-line growth.
543258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 8.4% YoY to INR397.9 crore, with EBITDA of INR91.7 crore (23.0% margin) and gross margin of 48.6% versus 47.4% a year earlier, despite raw material costs rising 50-100% in March 2026 due to the Middle East conflict. PAT fell to INR57.3 crore (14.4% margin) as treasury income dropped to INR0.19 crore on mark-to-market losses. For FY26, standalone revenue grew 4.1% to INR1,330 crore and PAT excluding a one-off gratuity provision grew 4% to INR149.8 crore. Management said it will accept roughly 200-250bp lower gross margin, with EBITDA margin broadly unchanged, to accelerate top-line growth in FY27. It also said no major capex is planned until FY29, with the Jodhpur water-based plant commissioning in June 2026.

segments.name: Paint categories (Q4 FY26 value growth / volume growth)
segments.commentary: Primers and distemper grew 14.9% value and 9.6% volume; putty and cement paint 12.6% value and 9.5% volume; emulsions 10.5% value and 11.2% volume; enamels and wood coatings 7.2% value and 5.4% volume. All four categories grew in value and volume.

segments.name: Apple Chemie (subsidiary, waterproofing)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR27.5 crore (+34.7% YoY); FY26 revenue INR75.1 crore (+17.8%). Gross margin around 40% plus/minus 1%. FY27 target is 30%-plus growth.

guidance_outlook: Management is prepared to accept a 2-2.5pp gross margin decline to drive faster top-line growth, while expecting EBITDA margin broadly unchanged.

Gross sales were growing double-digit for five consecutive months from November 2025, including March; the gap to reported net sales growth (8.5% in Q4) came from higher trade and influencer discounts netted off revenue.

Management said it is not guiding a specific net sales number for Q1 FY27 and expects net sales growth well above high-single-digit to low-double-digit levels over FY27, with the caveat that disruptions can set it back.
April growth was driven largely by price hikes; some dealer overstocking has occurred, so May-June demand is uncertain.
Industry price increases of about 12% on the overall basket were implemented; management does not foresee another significant price increase unless the Middle East situation deteriorates.
Management expects gross margins across the industry to normalise by Q2 FY27 as raw material costs stabilise, though Q1 may see volatility.
Apple Chemie targets 30%-plus revenue growth in FY27.
No major capex is envisaged until FY29; FCF is expected to step up from FY27 onwards. FY26 dividend proposed at INR5 per share, up 43% from INR3.5.
capex_capacity: Jodhpur water-based plant, 90,000 KL per annum capacity: final commissioning stage, trial production expected June 2026.
New solvent-based plant and expanded putty plant at Jodhpur have already commenced production in recent months.
Network at 31 March 2026: over 19,350 active dealers, over 12,200 tinting machines, 55 depots across all 28 states.
330 kW solar installation at Kochi factory is fully operational.
demand_pricing: Industry demand recovered from November 2025 after roughly 8 quarters of subdued growth; the Iran war from about March 2026 disrupted raw material supply and pushed some input prices up 50-100%.
The industry took about 12% price increases in three phases. Indigo's own unilateral price increase came around 24-25 March 2026, ahead of the market leader's 8 April increase.

Management said water-based paints are fully covered by price hikes; solvent-based enamels and wood coatings (about 17-18% of portfolio) have a small uncovered gap, partly offset by falling mineral turpentine oil prices.

543259|2026-06.headline: Home First Q1 FY27: AUM up 25.7% YoY to INR16,938 crore and PAT up 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, with stable asset quality.

Profit after tax rose 34.5% YoY to INR160 crore, driven by 38.2% growth in net interest income and NIM expanding to 6.0% from 5.9%. 543259|2026-09.headline: Home First Q2 FY27 AUM rose 27% YoY to Rs 18,010 crore and PAT grew 29.1% YoY to Rs 170 crore, with Stage 3 down to 1.7%.

Management reiterated a 5.0-5.2% spread commitment, a 25% AUM growth target for FY27 (Rs 20,000 crore by March 2027), and exit ROE targets of 15% (FY27) and 16% (FY28). 543260|2026-03.headline: Stove Kraft Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 32.4% YoY to INR414.5 crore, with PAT of INR6.1 crore and EBITDA margin of 9.5%.

543271|2026-09.headline: Jubilant Ingrevia Q2 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,394 crore and EBITDA 51% to INR221 crore; FY27 guidance reiterated, nearer upper end.

Management reiterated its FY27 guidance of INR750-800 crore (EBITDA basis as discussed on the call) and said it expects to land closer to the upper end, helped by a recent European competitor plant closure in acetic anhydride. The company also signed to acquire 40% of Zettaone Technologies for INR189 crore, entering electronics design and manufacturing services. rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 35–40% EBITDA margin for FY27–FY28 and Q1 FY27 margin above 40% with ~₹60 crore carry-over; FY26 margin was ~38% and Q4 dipped to ~27% on billing timing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 to Q4 FY27 (dredgers/hoppers within 90 days; shipyar
rows.why: FY27 capex of ₹400–500 crore incl. ~₹100 crore for the Saphale shipyard targeting 14 vessels/year, plus two dredgers and ~12,000 cu m hopper capacity addable in under 90 days; River Pearl 47 to run 240 days/year on rock tenders.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management projects ~30% revenue growth each year, backed by ~₹1,400 crore order book and ₹1,075 crore FY26 order inflow (vs ~₹201 crore to ₹256 crore revenue, ~27% growth in FY26).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has already guided ₹400–500 crore capex for FY27, with cash and debt as first funding source and equity only if needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Bid pipeline above ₹2,000 crore expected to convert in ~3 months and management flagged a fair chance of 40–41% EBITDA margin next year, but no formal upgrade has been given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 guide of >₹100 crore relies on ~₹60 crore of JNPA/Pondicherry single-payment revenue slipping from Q4; ₹16 crore Mangrol claim outstanding, debtor days above 45–60 day target, and ~₹114 crore short-term debt due in FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Green tugs for VOC Port and Visakhapatnam Port (~₹650 crore, 15-year tenure) to be fully built by mid-monsoon FY27, and export shipbuilding orders expected from Q3 or Q4 FY27 with yard designed for 14 vessels/year.

rows.label: Bid pipeline conversion above ₹2,000 crore
rows.why: Pipeline split ~₹950 crore dredging, ~₹400 crore shipbuilding, ~₹600 crore green tugs, with management expecting orders within three months, after ~₹1,075 crore FY26 inflow.

rows.label: Short-term debt repayment from accruals
rows.why: Short-term borrowings ~₹114 crore (JNPA short-tenure loan and others due in FY27) against cash in excess of ₹350 crore, of which ~₹300 crore is free after bank-guarantee lien.

rows.label: Debtor days and ₹16 crore Mangrol claim collection
rows.why: ₹16 crore outstanding on Mangrol dredging claim, with two of three additional claims received and debtor days above the 45–60 day target.

tone.note: Management was confident on the ₹1,075 crore order inflow, ₹1,400 crore order book, 30% growth and 35–40% margin guide, but turned defensive on the Q4 margin dip, ₹16 crore debtor claim, rising short-term debt and idle overseas vessels; analysts pressed on order slowdown and Q4 margins.
